definition_zh: 趋势；倾向；潮流；走向
definition_en: a general direction in which something is developing or changing over time
core_image: 纸上一条折线慢慢向上爬，旁边标着几个年份
scene: 办公室里，分析师把几年的销量画成折线，线在最后一段明显上扬。 The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
sceneCN: 这里 trend 是「趋势；走向」（第 1 个义项：事物随时间发展的总方向）；句意为销量的走势三年来一直在上升。纸上那条慢慢上扬的折线，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trend 加 -y 构成，义为「时髦的；赶潮流的」
由 trend 与 setter 复合，义为「引领潮流的人」
由 trend 加 -ing 构成，义为「正在流行的」

senses.title: The line on the graph
senses.definition: the general direction in which a situation is moving over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 情况在一段时间内发展的总方向
senses.example: The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 销量的走势三年来一直在上升。
senses.why: The word began as a turning of a river or a coast, and a line that keeps turning one way became a trend.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指河流或海岸的转弯，而一直朝一边转的线就成了趋势。

senses.title: What everyone is doing
senses.definition: a fashion or habit that many people take up at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时接受的时髦做法
senses.example: Short jackets are the trend this autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 短外套是今年秋天的潮流。
senses.why: When many people turn the same way at once, the direction looks like a fashion to follow.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时转向同一个方向，这个方向看起来就像可以追随的风尚。

senses.title: Leaning in one direction
senses.definition: to move or develop generally in a stated direction
senses.definitionCN: 大体朝某个方向移动或发展
senses.example: Prices trended downward through the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格趋于下降。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest picture: a course that keeps bending the same way.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了最古老的画面：一条一直朝同一方向弯的走向。

senses.title: Turning away from a fashion
senses.definition: to move away from a popular style in a new direction
senses.definitionCN: 离开流行样式，转向新的方向
senses.example: Designers are turning away from bright colours this year.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师今年正逐渐远离鲜亮的颜色。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old idea of a course bending, and fashion courses bend too.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留着航线折弯的旧意，时尚的走向同样会折弯。

intro.en: Trend first named the turning of a coastline or a river, and only later the direction of a set of figures.
intro.cn: trend 最初指海岸线或河流的转弯，后来才指一组数字的方向。

items.en: The verb trendan meant to turn or revolve, close to the modern tr-, dr- turn family.
items.cn: 古英语动词 trendan 意为转动、旋转，与表示「转」的词族相近。

items.en: A trend was the curve of a shore or the bend of a river.
items.cn: 中古英语里 trend 指海岸的弧线或河流的弯处。

items.en: Sailors spoke of the trend of a coast as its general direction.
items.cn: 水手用 the trend of a coast 指海岸的大致走向。

items.en: Statistics borrowed the word for the general direction of changing numbers.
items.cn: 统计学借用这个词，指变化中的数字的总方向。

items.en: Twentieth-century magazines applied it to fashion, giving the sense of a popular style.
items.cn: 二十世纪的杂志把它用在时尚上，产生了流行风潮的含义。

note.en: The first group shares the trend stem, the second holds other words for direction and fashion.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trend 词干，第二组收其他表示方向与流行的词。

entries.definition: Very fashionable.
Currently popular online.
A person who starts a fashion.
A leaning toward a kind of behaviour.
A popular style at a given time.
The line along which something moves.

normalIntro.en: Trend is a short word for a long line: the way things have been going and are likely to keep going.
normalIntro.cn: trend 是个短词，说的是长线：事情一路走来的方向，以及大概会继续走下去的方向。

normal.en: The verb is the same word: prices trend up.
normal.cn: 动词形式一模一样：prices trend up。

normal.en: The adjective trendy cuts the d and adds y.
normal.cn: 形容词 trendy 去掉 d 再加 y。

normal.en: A trendsetter sets the trend for others to follow.
normal.cn: trendsetter 设下潮流让旁人跟随。

normal.en: The plural is simply trends.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trends。

normal.en: Statistics made the word famous: a trend line on a chart.
normal.cn: 统计学让这个词流行：图表上的一条趋势线。

abstract.en: A coastline bending the same way for miles.
abstract.cn: 海岸线绵延数里朝同一方向弯。

abstract.en: Water finding one slope and staying with it.
abstract.cn: 水找到一面斜坡，就一路顺着它。

abstract.en: Many people turning their heads at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 许多人同时把头转向同一个方向。

examples.en: There is a clear trend toward smaller cars in the city.
examples.cn: 这座城市明显有偏爱小车的趋势。

examples.en: Rents in the old quarter have trended upward since spring.
examples.cn: 老城区的租金自春天以来趋于上涨。

examples.en: She never follows the fashion of the season.
examples.cn: 她从不追随当季的风尚。

dict_mnemonic.text: trend 里的 tren 一念就像「转」——大家往一个方向转，就成了潮流。

root: 古英语 trendan（转动），中古英语指海岸或河流的弯向，近代经统计学与时尚用语扩展为「趋势、潮流」；同族词有 trendy、trendsetter、trending。

sensesIntro.en: First the direction of a changing figure, then the fashion many follow, then the verb for moving that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是变化数字的方向，再是众人追随的时髦，最后是朝那个方向走的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bending line on a chart.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上弯曲的线。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers moving one way.
branches.cn: 数字分支：数字朝一个方向走。

branches.en: The fashion branch: many people turning together.
branches.cn: 时尚分支：许多人一起转向。

branches.en: The action branch: a course leaning one way.
branches.cn: 动作分支：走势朝一边倾。

branches.en: The chart branch: both are read on a line.
branches.cn: 图表分支：两者都在一条线上读出。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a habit becomes a general direction.
branches.cn: 人群分支：一种习惯变成总方向。

intro.en: Trend is a short Germanic stem that now builds compounds and derivatives in business and fashion.
intro.cn: trend 是短小的日耳曼语词干，如今在商业与时尚领域构成复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin; the Latin words below are cousins through shared Indo-European roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干并非拉丁语；下面的拉丁词只是通过共同印欧词根构成的远亲。

items.example: The stem works as noun and verb alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It forms trendy, full of fashion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trendy，满身时尚的。

items.example: It forms trending, popular right now.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trending，眼下正走红的。

items.example: The two words say what the person does.
items.exampleCN: 两个词直接说出这个人做的事。

items.example: Up names the direction of the line.
The line makes the direction visible.

definition_zh: 反向；颠倒；推翻；倒挡
definition_en: to change something to its opposite direction or order
core_image: 一条白色箭头在灰色地面上突然掉头，指向来路
scene: 他倒车时，发现灰色的小路尽头忽然出现了一片湖。 While he reversed the car, he found that a lake had suddenly appeared at the end of the gray lane.
sceneCN: 这里 reverse 是「倒车、使车辆后退」（第 1 个义项：向后移动）；句意：他倒车时，发现灰色的小路尽头忽然出现了一片湖。

derivatives.zh: 逆转；推翻
可逆的；双面的
不可逆的

senses.title: Going backwards
senses.definition: to move backwards or make a vehicle move backwards
senses.definitionCN: 向后移动，或使车辆向后行驶
senses.example: She reversed the car out of the driveway.
senses.exampleCN: 她把车倒出了车道。
senses.why: The prefix re- marks a backward movement.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 标记向后的运动。

senses.title: Opposite order
senses.definition: to change the order of things to the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 把事情顺序改为相反
senses.example: Please reverse the order of the two names.
senses.exampleCN: 请把这两个名字的顺序颠倒过来。
senses.why: Turning back can also mean turning a sequence around.
senses.whyCN: 转回去也可以指把顺序转过来。

senses.title: Complete change
senses.definition: to change a decision or situation to the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 把决定或局势改为相反
senses.example: The court reversed its earlier ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 法院推翻了先前的裁决。
senses.why: A decision can be turned back, just like a car.
senses.whyCN: 决定也能像车一样被掉转。

intro.en: Reverse comes from Latin revertere, to turn back, through Old French revers.
intro.cn: reverse 经法语 revers，源自拉丁语 revertere（转回）。

items.en: Revertere joins re-, back, and vertere, to turn.
items.cn: revertere 由 re-（回）与 vertere（转）组成。

items.en: Reversus is the past participle, meaning turned back.
items.cn: reversus 是过去分词，意为转回的。

items.en: Old French revers describes something turned the other way.
items.cn: 古法语 revers 描述转向另一边的事物。

items.en: Reverse enters English as both verb and noun.
items.cn: reverse 以动词和名词两种形式进入英语。

items.en: It comes to mean the opposite side or opposite order.
items.cn: 它逐渐指反面或相反的顺序。

note.en: Reverse turns back, while invert turns over.
note.cn: reverse 是转回去，invert 是翻转过来。

entries.definition: to return to a former state
the act of reversing
able to be reversed
to turn upside down
completely different
to cancel an action

normalIntro.en: Reverse is an arrow that turns around and points back.
normalIntro.cn: reverse 就是掉头、指回来的箭头。

normal.en: Reverse the car means drive it backward.
normal.cn: reverse the car 意为把车倒着开。

normal.en: In reverse order means from last to first.
normal.cn: in reverse order 意为从最后到最前。

normal.en: Reverse a decision means cancel and change it.
normal.cn: reverse a decision 意为撤销并改变决定。

normal.en: The reverse side is the back of something.
normal.cn: the reverse side 是某物的背面。

normal.en: Compare invert: invert flips over, reverse turns back.
normal.cn: 对比 invert：invert 是翻过来，reverse 是转回去。

abstract.en: Picture a one-way arrow pointing backwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指向后方的单向箭头。

abstract.en: Imagine reading a sentence from the last word to the first.
abstract.cn: 想象从最后一个词读到第一个词。

abstract.en: Think of a film playing in reverse.
abstract.cn: 想象电影倒着播放。

examples.en: She reversed the car into the garage.
examples.cn: 她把车倒进车库。

examples.en: The court reversed the earlier ruling.
examples.cn: 法院推翻了先前的裁决。

examples.en: The names are listed in reverse order.
examples.cn: 名字按相反顺序排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ verse（转）」——转回去，就是反向、颠倒；这只是拆词联想，与 verse（诗句）无关。

root: 拉丁语 revertere（转回）＝ re-（回）＋ vertere（转）→ 法语 revers → reverse，核心义「转回去、反过来」。

sensesIntro.en: Reverse starts with physical turning back, then moves to opposite order, and finally to changing a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: reverse 从身体上的转回开始，再引申为相反顺序，最后指改变决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white arrow turning back on gray ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色地面上的白色箭头掉头转向。

branches.en: Going backwards is the physical core.
branches.cn: 向后移动是物理层面的核心。

branches.en: Order can be turned around as well.
branches.cn: 顺序也能被调转。

branches.en: A decision can be reversed like a direction.
branches.cn: 决定可以像方向一样被推翻。

branches.en: The same turning motion applies to sequences.
branches.cn: 同样的转向也适用于顺序。

branches.en: Both order and decisions move to the opposite.
branches.cn: 顺序和决定都转向相反的一端。

intro.en: Reverse joins the prefix re-, back, to the Latin root vers, to turn.
intro.cn: reverse 由表示「回」的前缀 re- 与拉丁词根 vers（转）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, to turn, lies at the heart of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere（转）是这个词语的核心。

items.example: Reversible describes what can turn back.
items.exampleCN: reversible 描述可以反向的事物。

latinEntries.example: Vertere is the root of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vertere 是许多英语单词的词根。
revertere 在 vertere 前加 re-。

definition_zh: 错误；差错；误差
definition_en: a mistake, or the state of being wrong
core_image: 一支箭偏出靶心，落在旁边的空处
scene: 表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。 A small error in the table made the total wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 error 是「错误」（第 1 个义项：做错或写错的地方）；句意：表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。

derivatives.zh: 错误的
犯错；出错
无差错的

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done or written wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 做错或写错的事情
senses.example: She spotted an error in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现第一行有一个错误。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a wandering, so an error is a step that has strayed from the right way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词意为「游荡」，所以错误就是偏离正路的一步。

senses.title: The state of being wrong
senses.definition: the condition of holding a wrong belief or being mistaken
senses.definitionCN: 持有错误看法或弄错的状态
senses.example: I was in error about the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 我把会议时间弄错了。
senses.why: The word can name not only the mistake but the condition of being mistaken.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅指错误本身，也可以指弄错的状态。

senses.title: A measured deviation
senses.definition: a difference between a measured or calculated value and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算值与真实值之间的差异
senses.example: The experiment allows a small margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验允许有一个小的误差范围。
senses.why: Scientific use turns the general mistake into a measurable deviation.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把一般性的错误转化为可测量的偏差。

intro.en: Error comes from Latin error, a wandering or mistake, from errare, to wander.
intro.cn: error 来自拉丁语 error（游荡、错误），源于 errare（漫游）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or go astray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Errur carries the word into French.
items.cn: errur 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Error names a mistake in English.
items.cn: 中古英语 error 指错误。

items.en: Modern English adds scientific and computing errors.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了科学误差与计算机错误。

note.en: Error is the noun of straying, close to err, erroneous, and to ordinary mistake words.
note.cn: error 是表示「走偏」的名词，与 err、erroneous 以及普通的「错误」词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a mistake
wrong
wandering or straying
something done wrongly
a defect or responsibility for wrong
a small careless mistake

normalIntro.en: Error is a wandering step: the mind or hand leaves the straight road for a moment.
normalIntro.cn: error 是走偏的一步：头脑或手在一瞬间离开了直路。

normal.en: To make an error is to get something wrong.
normal.cn: make an error 就是把某事弄错。

normal.en: Human error causes many accidents.
normal.cn: 人为失误造成许多事故。

normal.en: An error message tells you the program failed.
normal.cn: error message 告诉你程序出错了。

normal.en: In error means by mistake.
normal.cn: in error 表示错误地。

normal.en: Compare mistake: mistake is everyday, error is slightly more formal and technical.
normal.cn: 对比 mistake：mistake 更日常，error 稍正式且更技术化。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow landing just beside the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭落在靶心旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a pen slipping on a single letter.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖在一个字母上滑了一下。

abstract.en: Think of a clock running a few seconds fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟快了几秒钟。

examples.en: The report contains several spelling errors.
examples.cn: 报告里有几处拼写错误。

examples.en: He sent the parcel to the wrong address in error.
examples.cn: 他误把包裹寄到了错误的地址。

examples.en: Scientists try to reduce the margin of error.
examples.cn: 科学家努力缩小误差范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「err + or」——走「偏」了，就是犯错；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（游荡；错误）→ 古法语 errur → 英语 error，核心义「偏离正途」。

sensesIntro.en: Error first means a wrong act or word, then the state of being mistaken, and finally a measurable deviation.
sensesIntro.cn: error 先指做错的事或写错的地方，再指弄错的状态，最后指可测量的误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that lands beside the target.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭落在靶心旁边。

branches.en: A concrete mistake is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 具体的错误是日常义项。

branches.en: Being mistaken is the state sense.
branches.cn: 弄错的状态是状态义项。

branches.en: A measured deviation is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 测量偏差是技术义项。

branches.en: A person in error often makes a visible mistake.
branches.cn: 处于错误中的人往往会犯下可见的错误。

branches.en: Both a slip and a margin of error are deviations from the true value.
branches.cn: 小失误与误差范围都是对真实值的偏离。

intro.en: Error is a Latin wandering noun, with English err, erroneous, and errorless built around it.
intro.cn: error 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的名词，英语围绕它构成 err、erroneous 与 errorless。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

items.example: Err is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: err 是简短的英语动词。

definition_zh: 频道；渠道；通道；海峡
definition_en: a television or radio station, a passage through which water or information moves, or a narrow stretch of sea
core_image: 一条被水流长期冲出的窄沟
scene: 山谷深处的岩壁被水磨得光滑。 The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 channel 指「水道；通道」（第 2 个义项：水或其他事物通过的路径）；句意是河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。

derivatives.zh: 多频道的；多渠道的
渠道化；开渠

senses.title: A television or radio band
senses.definition: a band of frequencies used by a particular television or radio station
senses.definitionCN: 某家电视台或电台使用的频段
senses.example: Switch to another channel after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻结束后换到另一个频道。
senses.why: Broadcasting needed a word for a path that carries a signal, and the waterway word supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 广播需要一个表示信号通路的词，而水道这个词正好补上。

senses.title: A passage for water or information
senses.definition: a passage through which water, goods or information moves
senses.definitionCN: 水、货物或信息通过的路径
senses.example: The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。
senses.why: The Latin base meant a pipe or groove, the exact shape of any narrow passage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基意为管道或沟槽，正是任何狭窄通道的形状。

senses.title: A narrow sea passage
senses.definition: a narrow stretch of water between two areas of land
senses.definitionCN: 两片陆地之间的狭长水域
senses.example: Ships waited for calm weather to cross the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 船只等待风平浪静时穿越海峡。
senses.why: A groove filled with sea water is simply the waterway sense on a map-sized scale.
senses.whyCN: 灌满海水的沟槽，不过是水道义在地图尺度上的放大。

intro.en: Channel goes back to a Latin word for a pipe, and every later sense keeps that shape of a narrow passage.
intro.cn: channel 可追溯到拉丁语表示管道的词，后来各义项都保留狭窄通路这一形状。

items.en: Canalis meant a pipe, groove or water channel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 意为管道、沟槽或水道。

items.en: Chanel named a bed of a stream or a narrow sea passage.
items.cn: chanel 指河床或狭窄的海上通道。

items.en: English channel first described a watercourse and a strait.
items.cn: 英语 channel 先描述水道与海峡。

items.en: The word extended to any route by which something travels.
items.cn: 该词扩展到任何事物通行的路线。

items.en: Radio and television gave it the sense of a broadcast band.
items.cn: 广播与电视赋予它播出频段的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the canal shape, while the meaning group lists other passages and routes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 canal 的外形，近义组列出其他通道与路线。

entries.definition: a man-made waterway
the area around the altar of a church
more than one channel
a way through something
a way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处的路线

entries.definition: a narrow passage of water

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the canal root, the sea strait and the phrase through official channels.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 canal 词根、海峡义以及短语 through official channels。

normal.en: Channel and canal are twins from the Latin word for a pipe.
normal.cn: channel 与 canal 是拉丁语「管道」一词的双胞胎。

normal.en: A television channel is a groove cut for a signal instead of water.
normal.cn: 电视频道就是为信号而非水流开出的沟。

normal.en: Through official channels means by the proper route, not by a shortcut.
normal.cn: through official channels 意为走正规路线，而非抄近路。

normal.en: The English Channel is simply the waterway sense written on a map.
normal.cn: the English Channel 不过是水道义写在地图上。

normal.en: The verb channel takes resources as its object, as in channel funds into schools.
normal.cn: 动词 channel 以资源为宾语，如 channel funds into schools。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow groove in stone with water running through it.
abstract.cn: 想象石头上一条窄沟，水从中流过。

abstract.en: Picture a remote control clicking from one station to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象遥控器从一个台跳到下一个台。

abstract.en: Picture ships queuing between two headlands in grey weather.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗天气里船只在两处海角间排队。

examples.en: The interview will be shown on channel four.
examples.cn: 这次采访将在第四频道播出。

examples.en: Complaints should go through the proper channels.
examples.cn: 投诉应通过正当渠道提出。

examples.en: They channelled the extra money into research.
examples.cn: 他们把额外的钱投入研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 channel 想成 canal（运河）：运河是水的频道，电视频道是信号的运河。

root: 源自拉丁语 canalis（管道、沟槽），经古法语 chanel 进入英语；与 canal 同源，核心形状是狭长的通路。

sensesIntro.en: A groove for water becomes a passage for goods and news, a strait on the map and a band for broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 流水的沟槽变成货物与消息的通道，再变成地图上的海峡与播出的频段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow groove that carries something along.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把某物往前输送的窄沟。

branches.en: A broadcast band is a channel for a signal.
branches.cn: 播出频段是信号的通道。

branches.en: A river channel is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 河道是最古老也最具体的义项。

branches.en: A strait is a channel at the scale of a map.
branches.cn: 海峡是地图尺度上的通道。

branches.en: Both keep the image of water finding a narrow way.
branches.cn: 两者都保留水寻找窄路的意象。

branches.en: Information now flows where water once flowed.
branches.cn: 如今信息在昔日水流之处流动。

intro.en: Channel keeps the -canal- root in canal, channelization and multichannel.
intro.cn: channel 在 canal、channelization 与 multichannel 中保留 -canal- 词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin canalis is the pipe that gave both channel and canal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 就是给出 channel 与 canal 的那根管道。

items.example: The channel was full of mud.
They channelled water to the field.
She is channelling her energy into work.
Canalis is the old pipe word.
The tunnel runs under the river.

latinEntries.exampleCN: canalis 在法语中变成 chanel。

latinEntries.example: Canal is the twin of channel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: canal 是 channel 的双胞胎。

definition_zh: 一贯的；前后一致的；与…相符的
definition_en: always behaving or happening in the same way, or in agreement with something
core_image: 一条笔直的刻度线，从头到尾没有偏移
scene: 教练翻看整季的记录，发现队员的状态几乎没有起伏。 Her consistent effort finally paid off.
sceneCN: 这里 consistent 指「一贯的」（第 1 个义项：长期保持同样的标准）；句意是她一贯的努力终于有了回报。

pos.zh: 一贯的；前后一致的；与…相符的

derivatives.zh: 一致性；连贯性
一贯地；始终如一地
不一致；前后矛盾
由…组成；在于

senses.title: Staying the same
senses.definition: keeping the same standard or pattern over time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间里保持同样的标准或做法
senses.example: Her grades were consistent all year.
senses.exampleCN: 她全年的成绩一直很稳定。
senses.why: A pattern only becomes visible when it repeats without breaking.
senses.whyCN: 只有不被打断地重复，一种做法才会显出形状。

senses.title: In agreement
senses.definition: matching another fact, rule or account
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事实、规则或说法相吻合
senses.example: His story is consistent with the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与证据相符。
senses.why: Two pieces of a puzzle are trusted when their edges fit.
senses.whyCN: 拼图的两块只有边对得上，才让人相信。

senses.title: Steady in quality
senses.definition: holding the same quality or texture without sudden change
senses.definitionCN: 质地或品质保持不变，没有突然的波动
senses.example: The sauce has a consistent texture.
senses.exampleCN: 这酱汁的质地很均匀。
senses.why: Hands and tongues notice a single lump at once.
senses.whyCN: 手和舌头一下子就能察觉出那一点疙瘩。

intro.en: Consistent comes from Latin consistens, the present participle of consistere, to stand firm together.
intro.cn: consistent 来自拉丁语 consistens，是 consistere（一起站稳）的现在分词。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and sistere meant to take a stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，sistere 意为站定。

items.en: Consistere described things holding their place together.
items.cn: consistere 描述事物一起守住各自的位置。

items.en: Consistens named whatever stood firm without shifting.
items.cn: consistens 指稳稳站住、不肯移动的事物。

items.en: French consistant used the word for firm and solid things.
items.cn: 法语 consistant 用它形容坚实不散的东西。

items.en: English consistent moved from physical firmness to steady behaviour.
items.cn: 英语 consistent 从实体的坚固转向行为的稳定。

items.en: It now chiefly means agreeing with itself or with the facts.
items.cn: 如今它主要指与自身或与事实相符。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin stand base, and the meaning group names other words for a pattern that does not break.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的站立词基，近义组列出其他表示「不中断的做法」的词。

entries.definition: to be made up of particular parts
to demand something firmly
to continue in spite of difficulty
developing or moving at an even rate
happening all the time without a pause
the same in all its parts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from parts that keep standing in place, then move to two edges that fit and to an even texture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从守在原位的各部分开始，再到对得上的两条边，最后到均匀的质地。

normal.en: Con- is together and sist is stand, so consistent is standing together without slipping.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sist 是站立，consistent 就是一起站住而不滑动。

normal.en: A ruler with no bent mark: that is a consistent record.
normal.cn: 一把没有任何弯折刻度的尺子，就是一贯的记录。

normal.en: Two puzzle edges that fit mean the accounts are consistent.
normal.cn: 两块拼图的边能对上，就说明两种说法彼此相符。

normal.en: Consistent effort is boring to watch and hard to beat.
normal.cn: 一贯的努力看着乏味，却很难被击败。

normal.en: Say the same true thing on a good day and a bad day.
normal.cn: 在顺境和逆境里说同一句真话。

abstract.en: Picture a compass drawing the same circle twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一把圆规把同一个圆画了两遍。

abstract.en: Picture a row of bricks all set at the same height.
abstract.cn: 想象一排砖都砌在同一高度。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat line that keeps an even rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一条保持均匀节奏的心跳线。

examples.en: The team showed consistent improvement over the season.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在整个赛季里稳步提高。

examples.en: Her answer was consistent with the facts.
examples.cn: 她的回答与事实相符。

examples.en: He is consistent in the way he treats people.
examples.cn: 他待人接物的方式始终如一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consistent 记成 con（一起）加 sist（站立）加 ent：始终站在同一个位置不动，就是一贯的、前后一致的。

root: 源自拉丁语 consistere（com 一起 + sistere 站立）的现在分词 consistens，本义是稳稳站住，后指一贯不变与前后相符。

sensesIntro.en: From a pattern that never shifts, to two accounts that fit, and finally to an even texture you can feel.
sensesIntro.cn: 从从不改变的做法，到彼此吻合的两种说法，最后到手上能摸出的均匀质地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line of marks with no gap and no tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排笔直的刻度，既不断裂也不倾斜。

branches.en: The first sense is a habit repeated until it looks like a line.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是重复到成一条线的习惯。

branches.en: The second sense judges whether two accounts share an edge.
branches.cn: 第二个义项判断两种说法是否共享同一条边。

branches.en: The third sense is evenness you can feel with hand or tongue.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是手或舌头能感到的均匀。

branches.en: Both senses ask whether something would look the same on a second look.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在问：再看一遍是否还是这个样子。

branches.en: A steady hand and a steady sauce both refuse sudden change.
branches.cn: 稳定的手与均匀的酱汁都拒绝突然的变化。

intro.en: Consistent is built on Latin con-, together, plus sistere, to stand, with the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: consistent 由拉丁语 con-（一起）、sistere（站立）与形容词词尾 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stand base sist- also appears in insist, persist and resist, and the -ent ending marks a quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的站立词基 sist- 也出现在 insist、persist 与 resist 中，而 -ent 词尾表示一种性质。

items.meaning: standing together in the same way
items.meaningCN: 以同样的方式站在一起

items.meaning: to be made up of parts
items.example: The team consists of four people.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队由四个人组成。

items.meaning: in the same way every time
the state of staying the same
not staying the same or not fitting
to stand firmly on a demand
items.example: They insisted on a written reply.
She resisted the urge to shout.

definition_zh: 就业；工作；雇用；使用
definition_en: the state of having paid work, or the act of hiring someone
core_image: 一份签好的工作合同，意味着稳定的收入
scene: 毕业后她找到了一份稳定的工作。 After graduation she found steady employment.
sceneCN: 这里 employment 是「就业」（第 1 个义项：拥有有薪工作的状态）；句意：毕业后她找到了一份稳定的工作。

derivatives.zh: 失业
自雇；个体经营

senses.title: The state of having paid work
senses.definition: the condition of having a job that pays wages or a salary
senses.definitionCN: 拥有一份支付工资或薪水的工作的状态
senses.example: The country aims for full employment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家追求充分就业。
senses.why: The noun names the condition produced by being employed, so it points to steady paid work.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名被雇用后产生的状态，因此指向稳定的有薪工作。

senses.title: A job or occupation
senses.definition: a particular job or kind of work someone does
senses.definitionCN: 某人所从事的特定工作或职业
senses.example: Teaching is her main employment.
senses.exampleCN: 教书是她的主要工作。
senses.why: The state of being employed becomes concrete as the job itself.
senses.whyCN: 被雇用的状态具体化，就变成了工作本身。

senses.title: The act of using something
senses.definition: the formal use of a tool, method, or word
senses.definitionCN: 对工具、方法或词语的正式使用
senses.example: The employment of simple tools saved time.
senses.exampleCN: 使用简单工具节省了时间。
senses.why: The older sense of putting something to work survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 把某物投入使用的古老含义在正式写作中保留下来。

intro.en: Employment adds the noun ending -ment to employ, naming both the state and the act.
intro.cn: employment 在 employ 后加名词词尾 -ment，既命名状态也命名行为。

items.en: Employer supplies the verb that English later expands.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 提供了英语后来扩展的动词。

items.en: Employ enters English with senses of use and occupation.
items.cn: employ 带着使用与占用的含义进入英语。

items.en: The noun employment appears for both work and use.
items.cn: 名词 employment 出现，兼指工作与使用。

items.en: Employment becomes a key word in economics and law.
items.cn: 在工业时代，employment 成为经济与法律的关键词。

items.en: Employment now chiefly means paid work.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employment 主要指有薪工作。

note.en: Employment is the state or the job; work is the activity, and occupation is the profession.
note.cn: employment 是状态或工作，work 是活动，occupation 是职业。

entries.definition: a person who is paid to work
a person or company that hires workers
to hire or use
paid work for an employer
activity done to achieve a result
a person's profession

normalIntro.en: Employment is the -ment noun of employ: the state of working and the job itself.
normalIntro.cn: employment 是 employ 的 -ment 名词：工作的状态与工作本身。

normal.en: Full employment means almost everyone has work.
normal.cn: full employment 意味着几乎人人有工作。

normal.en: An employment contract protects both sides.
normal.cn: employment contract 保护双方。

normal.en: She seeks employment in a new city.
normal.cn: 她在新城市求职。

normal.en: Unemployment is the opposite state.
normal.cn: unemployment 是相反的状态。

normal.en: The employment rate measures paid work.
normal.cn: employment rate 衡量有薪工作。

abstract.en: Picture a signed contract on a clean desk.
abstract.cn: 想象干净桌面上签好的合同。

abstract.en: See a line of people entering an office at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨人们走进办公室的队伍。

abstract.en: Think of steady pay arriving each month.
abstract.cn: 想象每个月按时到账的工资。

examples.en: The country aims for full employment.
examples.cn: 这个国家追求充分就业。

examples.en: Teaching is her main employment.
examples.cn: 教书是她的主要工作。

examples.en: The employment of simple tools saved time.
examples.cn: 使用简单工具节省了时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因普劳伊门特」——被公司请进门、有活干的状态；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: employ 加名词词尾 -ment，词根源自拉丁语 implicare。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the state of working, the job itself, and the formal use of something.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖工作状态、工作本身，以及正式使用某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed contract that guarantees steady pay.
core.cn: 核心意象：保证稳定收入的已签合同。

branches.en: The base sense is the state of having paid work.
branches.cn: 基本义是拥有有薪工作的状态。

branches.en: The state becomes concrete as a job.
branches.cn: 状态具体化为一份工作。

branches.en: The older sense of use survives in formal contexts.
branches.cn: 较古老的使用义在正式语境中保留。

branches.en: Having work and holding a job describe one reality.
branches.cn: 有工作和拥有一份工作描述同一现实。

branches.en: A job is work put to steady use.
branches.cn: 一份工作就是被稳定使用的劳动。

intro.en: Employment is employ plus -ment, turning the verb into a noun of state.
intro.cn: employment 是 employ 加 -ment，把动词变成状态名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root plic-, to fold, runs through employ, employee, and employment.
latinIntro.cn: 意为折叠的拉丁词根 plic- 贯穿 employ、employee 与 employment。

items.example: Employ is the base of employment.
items.exampleCN: employ 是 employment 的基础。

items.example: A job is a form of employment.
items.exampleCN: 一份工作是就业的一种形式。

definition_zh: 喉咙；咽喉；嗓门；窄口
definition_en: the passage at the back of the mouth that carries food to the stomach and air to the lungs
core_image: 一条细窄的通道，从口腔往里，食物和空气都要挤过这里
scene: 唱了整晚的歌,第二天早上他几乎说不出话来。 My throat is so sore that I can hardly speak this morning.
sceneCN: 这里 throat 是「喉咙」（第 1 个义项：口腔后方的通道）；句意为今早我喉咙痛得几乎说不出话。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「喉音的；沙哑的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，多用于复合词，义为「有……喉的」

senses.title: The passage inside the neck
senses.definition: the front of the neck and the passage inside it, through which food and air pass
senses.definitionCN: 颈部前侧及其内部、食物与空气经过的通道
senses.example: He had a sore throat and stayed in bed all day.
senses.exampleCN: 他喉咙痛，一整天都待在床上。
senses.why: The root meant to swell, and the throat is the swollen-looking passage in the neck.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「膨胀」，喉咙就是颈中那条看上去鼓起的通道。

senses.title: The voice, informally
senses.definition: the voice, especially its quality or strength, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 指嗓音，尤指其音质或力度，多用于口语
senses.example: She has a good throat for singing folk songs.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱起民歌来有一副好嗓子。
senses.why: The passage that makes voice is easily named for the voice itself.
senses.whyCN: 造就声音的通道很容易被直接用来称呼声音本身。

senses.title: A narrow opening
senses.definition: a narrow entrance or passage, such as the throat of a bottle
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄的入口或通道，如瓶颈
senses.example: The throat of the bottle was too narrow for the brush.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶口太窄，刷子伸不进去。
senses.why: The body image is transferred outward: any narrow passage in an object is its throat.
senses.whyCN: 身体的意象被移到体外：任何器物的窄通道都是它的「喉」。

senses.title: The narrow land between areas
senses.definition: a narrow strip of land or water forming a passage between two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长陆地或水道
senses.example: The valley is the throat of the northern trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷是北方商路的咽喉。
senses.why: The body image moves outward once more: narrow land between wide regions is a throat.
senses.whyCN: 身体意象再一次移到体外：宽广区域之间的狭长陆地也是一道咽喉。

intro.en: Throat comes from Old English, and the root behind it meant to swell, which describes the bulge of the neck.
intro.cn: throat 来自古英语，其词根意为「膨胀」，正是对颈部鼓起之形的描述。

items.en: The Germanic root for swelling or puffing up lies behind the word, a picture of the rising front of the neck.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「膨胀、鼓起」的词根是其来源，正是颈前隆起之形。

items.en: Old English þrote named the front of the neck and the gullet, both the outside and the passage.
items.cn: 古英语 þrote 兼指颈前与外食管，内外两面都包括。

items.en: Middle English throat settled the spelling, and the word kept both the outer neck and the inner passage.
items.cn: 中古英语固定了 throat 的拼写，并保留颈外与颈内通道两义。

items.en: Modern English added the transferred use for narrow openings, from bottles to valleys.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了移用义，指从瓶口到山谷的各种窄口。

items.en: Idioms about clearing, cutting or forcing down the throat keep the body image alive in everyday speech.
items.cn: 关于清嗓、割喉、强灌的习语让这个身体意象在日常口语中一直鲜活。

note.en: The first group separates the throat family from its near spellings; the second compares body passages and narrow openings.
note.cn: 第一组区分 throat 词族与形近词；第二组比较身体通道与窄口。

entries.definition: Deep and rough in voice, as if from the throat.
To send something through the air; it sounds the same at the start but has another root.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷；开头读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: Used in compounds such as white-throated, describing the throat of a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 white-throated 一类复合词，描述鸟的喉部

entries.definition: From one side to the other; one letter shape apart from throat.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 throat 拼写形近

entries.definition: The tube from the throat to the stomach; the medical word for the inner passage.
entries.definitionCN: 食管（喉到胃的管内通道，医学用词）

entries.definition: The voice box at the top of the throat.
The whole part joining head and body, with the throat at its front.
A valve controlling an engine, originally the throat of the pipe.
entries.definitionCN: 节流阀（原指管子的喉部，与 throat 同源）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the swelling root, the narrow-passage image and the idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「膨胀」词根、窄通道意象，以及相关习语。

normal.en: The root meant to swell; the throat is the swelling front of the neck.
normal.cn: 词根意为「膨胀」；喉咙就是颈前鼓起的那部分。

normal.en: A sore throat is the everyday complaint that names the passage directly.
normal.cn: a sore throat 是最日常的说法，直接点名那条通道。

normal.en: Clear your throat, not your through: the two words look alike.
normal.cn: 是 clear your throat，不是 through：两个词长得像。

normal.en: Throttle shares the root: it was the throat of a pipe before it was a valve.
normal.cn: throttle 同源：它先是管子的喉部，后来才成了阀门。

normal.en: A bottle has a throat, and so does a mountain valley.
normal.cn: 瓶子有喉咙，山谷也有咽喉。

abstract.en: Picture everything going in and out of the body having to squeeze through one narrow gate.
abstract.cn: 想象进出身体的一切都必须挤过同一道窄门。

abstract.en: The word is the narrowness itself: inner passage, voice, bottle mouth or mountain pass.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是「窄」本身：内通道、嗓音、瓶口或山口。

abstract.en: Speak of the throat and you speak of the bottleneck of every body.
abstract.cn: 提到喉咙，就提到每具身体的瓶颈。

examples.en: He cleared his throat before beginning the speech.
examples.cn: 他清了下嗓子才开始讲话。

examples.en: A cold can leave you with a sore throat.
examples.cn: 感冒可能会让你喉咙痛。

examples.en: The boat slipped through the throat of the harbour.
examples.cn: 小船驶过了港口的咽喉水道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思漏特」——一想到这里就紧张，喉咙漏风说不出话 → throat 喉咙

root: 古英语 þrote，源自日耳曼词根「膨胀、鼓起」，本指颈前隆起处及其内通道；今兼指嗓音、器物窄口与地形要隘，同源词 throttle 原即「管喉」。

sensesIntro.en: Throat is the body’s narrow gateway, and the same narrowness is lent to the voice, to bottles and to mountain passes.
sensesIntro.cn: throat 是身体的窄门，这份「窄」又被借给嗓音、瓶口与山口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything entering and leaving the body squeezing through one narrow gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：进出身体的一切都挤过同一道窄门。

branches.en: The body: the passage for air and food.
branches.cn: 身体线：空气与食物共用的通道。

branches.en: The sound: the throat standing for the voice.
branches.cn: 声音线：喉咙代指嗓音。

branches.en: The object: neck of a bottle, throat of a pipe.
branches.cn: 器物线：瓶颈、管喉。

branches.en: The landscape: a valley or strait as a passage.
branches.cn: 地形线：作为通道的山谷或海峡。

branches.en: Inside and outside narrowness share one image.
branches.cn: 体内的「窄」与器物的「窄」共用同一意象。

intro.en: Throat forms a -y adjective and takes -s; its older relative throttle already carries the narrow-throat image.
intro.cn: throat 可加 -y 构成形容词并加 -s，同源词 throttle 已带有「窄喉」意象。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它构成复合词里的 throated。

items.example: The larynx holds the vocal cords.

definition_zh: 生物；动物；人（带怜爱或轻蔑语气）
definition_en: a living animal or person, especially one shaped by nature
core_image: 草丛里一双发亮的眼睛盯着你，看不出那是什么
scene: 夜里草丛忽然一动，一双眼睛反着月光。 Something small and alive was moving in the grass, a creature we could not name.
sceneCN: 这里 creature 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：有生命的动物或人）；句意是草丛里有种小小的活物在动，一种我们叫不出名字的生物。

derivatives.zh: 创造
创造；创作物
有创造力的
创造者

senses.title: A living being
senses.definition: a living animal or person
senses.definitionCN: 有生命的动物或人
senses.example: Every creature needs water and air.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个生物都需要水和空气。
senses.why: Life is what all breathing things share.
senses.whyCN: 凡是会呼吸的东西，都共享生命。

senses.title: An animal
senses.definition: an animal, especially a small or unfamiliar one
senses.definitionCN: 动物，尤指微小或不熟悉的动物
senses.example: The pond is full of tiny creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里满是微小的生物。
senses.why: A word is needed for animals too small to name.
senses.whyCN: 总得有个词来称呼小到叫不出名字的动物。

senses.title: A person, with pity
senses.definition: a person, spoken of with pity or contempt
senses.definitionCN: 带着怜悯或轻蔑去说一个人
senses.example: The poor creature had nowhere to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 这个可怜的人无处可睡。
senses.why: People are living things too, so the word can carry pity.
senses.whyCN: 人也是活物，所以这个词能带上怜悯。

intro.en: Creature comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatura, a thing made.
intro.cn: creature 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatura（被造之物）进入英语。

items.en: Creare meant to make something grow or come forth.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生长或出现。

items.en: Creatura named anything that had been brought into being.
items.cn: creatura 指一切被带进存在之中的东西。

items.en: Creature named a created living thing.
items.cn: creature 指被创造的活物。

items.en: Creature first meant any being made by God.
items.cn: creature 最初指上天所造的任何存在。

items.en: It now usually means an animal, or a person seen with pity.
items.cn: 今天它通常指动物，或带着怜悯去看的一个人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the meaning group names other living things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 这个词干，近义组列出其他表示生命体的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new
the act of making something
a person who makes something
a living thing that is not a plant
anything that is alive
a single living body

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a shape in the grass and end with a face you almost know.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从草丛里的一个影子开始，最后落到一张你几乎认得的脸。

normal.en: Create plus -ure: something created and left alive.
normal.cn: create 加 -ure：被造出来又活着的东西。

normal.en: Four legs, two eyes, one warm body.
normal.cn: 四条腿，两只眼，一具温热的身体。

normal.en: If it moves by itself, it is a creature.
normal.cn: 能自己动的东西，就是生物。

normal.en: A creature keeps no diary; it just keeps breathing.
normal.cn: 生物不写日记，它只管呼吸。

normal.en: Call it a creature when you cannot name the animal.
normal.cn: 叫不出名字时，就称它一声生物。

abstract.en: Picture eyes shining in a dark hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗树篱里发亮的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a shell moving slowly across wet sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只壳在湿沙上缓缓移动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that is not quite human.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不太像人的手。

examples.en: A small creature ran across the path.
examples.cn: 一只小生物跑过小路。

examples.en: The cave is home to creatures that avoid light.
examples.cn: 这洞穴是避光生物的家。

examples.en: She treats every creature with care.
examples.cn: 她对每个生灵都很爱护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creature 记成 create（创造）加 -ure：被造出来、还会自己动的东西，就是生物。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生长），经 creatura（被造之物）而来；本义是「被造出来的活物」，后专指动物，也可带感情地指人。

sensesIntro.en: From any living thing, to an animal, to a person spoken of with feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何活物，到动物，再到带着感情去说的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bright eyes in the grass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里草丛中两点发亮的眼睛。

branches.en: Anything alive and breathing is a creature.
branches.cn: 一切活着会呼吸的都是生物。

branches.en: Small animals are the creatures we meet most often.
branches.cn: 小动物是我们最常遇到的生物。

branches.en: A person can be called a creature when we feel pity.
branches.cn: 心里怜悯时，人可以被称为生物。

branches.en: The same word covers a beetle and a beggar.
branches.cn: 同一个词既盖住甲虫，也盖住乞丐。

branches.en: An unnamed animal is simply a creature in the dark.
branches.cn: 叫不出名的动物，就是黑暗里的一只生物。

intro.en: Creature belongs to the Latin family of creare, to make, which also gives create and creation.
intro.cn: creature 属于拉丁语 creare（制造）这一族，create 与 creation 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root creare, to bring forth, runs through the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 creare（使产生）贯穿这一整族词。

items.example: The creature slept in the leaves.
They create a new game each week.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周造一个新游戏。

items.meaning: the act or result of making

items.exampleCN: 她有一颗善于创造的心。

items.meaning: in the manner of a creature
items.exampleCN: 它带着生物般的谨慎移动。
粗心的手把形状造坏了。

definition_zh: 改变；改动；使不同；（按尺寸）改衣服；给（动物）做绝育手术；另一个自我
definition_en: to make something or someone different, to adjust a garment so that it fits, to neuter an animal, or, in the phrase alter ego, a second self
core_image: 裁缝的粉线在旧衣上重新划过，同一块布被改成另一个样子
scene: 裁缝铺里，一件旧大衣挂在镜子前，两只袖口明显太长。 She altered the sleeves so that the coat finally fitted her.
sceneCN: 这里 alter 是「按尺寸改衣服」（第 2 个义项：为合身而修改衣物）；句意为她把袖子改短，大衣终于合身了。画面里是镜子、粉线与针线盒。

pos.zh: 及物动词：改变；改动；修改（衣服）；给（动物）绝育

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「改动；修改」，尤指改衣
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可改变的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 alterable 构成，义为「无法改变的」
由拉丁语 alter 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「他者性；相异性」，多用于哲学与文化研究

senses.title: To make something different
senses.definition: to make a thing or a person different in some way, without replacing it with something else
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式使某物或某人变得不同，而不是把它整个换成别的东西
senses.example: Nothing can alter the fact that the deadline has already passed.
senses.exampleCN: 截止时间已经过去，这个事实无法改变。
senses.why: Latin alter means the other of two, so the verb first pictured making a thing into that other version of itself rather than swapping it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，动词最初想的正是把一样东西变成它自己的另一个版本，而不是换掉它，所以核心含义是「使不同」。

senses.title: To adjust a garment to fit
senses.definition: to take in, let out or otherwise adjust a piece of clothing so that it fits better
senses.definitionCN: 把衣物收进、放出或以其他方式调整，使其更合身
senses.example: The tailor altered the waist of the skirt in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝一个下午就把裙子的腰身改好了。
senses.why: Cloth is the most concrete thing one can make other: the fabric stays, but its shape is turned into another fit.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是最具体的「把一样东西变成另一个样子」：布料还是那块布，形状却被改成另一种合身状态，所以裁缝的改动也用 alter。

senses.title: To become different
senses.definition: to change by itself over time, without any outside agent doing it
senses.definitionCN: 随时间自行改变，而不是由外部力量施加改动
senses.example: The town has altered little since the railway closed.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路停运以来，这座小镇几乎没有变化。
senses.why: Used without an object, the same pushing of a thing toward its other version lands on the subject itself.
senses.whyCN: 当动词不带宾语时，那股「把东西推向另一个版本」的力量就落在主语自己身上，于是从「改变别的东西」变成「自身发生变化」。

senses.title: A second self
senses.definition: in the phrase alter ego, a second self, a trusted other personality, or a role a person adopts
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 alter ego，指第二自我、可信赖的另一个人格，或一个人扮演的角色
senses.example: On stage he adopts an alter ego who is loud and fearless.
senses.exampleCN: 在舞台上他会变成另一个自我，嗓门很大，无所畏惧。
senses.why: Alter ego is Latin for other I, and the phrase keeps the original sense of the other one of a pair in its purest form.
senses.whyCN: alter ego 是拉丁语「另一个我」，把「两者中的另一个」这个本义原封不动地保留下来，所以指第二人格或另一个自己。

senses.title: To neuter an animal
senses.definition: to remove the reproductive organs of a pet or farm animal so that it cannot breed
senses.definitionCN: 切除宠物或家畜的生殖器官，使其不能繁殖
senses.example: The shelter alters every cat before it is offered for adoption.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所给每只猫做完绝育手术才让人领养。
senses.why: The animal's body is made into another state that cannot breed, which is the same core idea reaching a use far from tailoring.
senses.whyCN: 动物的身体被改造成另一种不能繁殖的状态，同一个核心意象延伸到一个与衣服无关的用途，这是美国英语里的常见说法。

intro.en: Alter came into English from Latin through French, and its oldest meaning is simply the other one of two.
intro.cn: alter 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，最古老的意思不过是「两者中的另一个」。

items.en: *h₂el- is generally reconstructed as meaning beyond or other; the same root is thought to lie behind Latin alius and English else.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *h₂el- 表示「在……之外、另一个」；拉丁语 alius 与英语 else 也一般认为出自这个词根。

items.en: Alter meant the other of two, as opposed to alius, which meant another among more than two.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，与表示「两者以上之中的另一个」的 alius 相对。

items.en: Alter plus the verb ending -are gave alterare, to make different or change.
items.cn: alter 加上动词词尾 -are 构成 alterare，意为「使不同、改变」。

items.en: Old French alterer carried the verb into English; the medical and legal branches did not come with it.
items.cn: 古法语 alterer 把这个动词带入英语，医学与法律的分支并没有随之而来。

items.en: The tailoring sense is recorded in the nineteenth century, and alter ego was borrowed whole from Latin in the sixteenth; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 改衣义在十九世纪有记录，alter ego 则在十六世纪整条短语从拉丁语借入；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin alter family and one phrase borrowed whole; the near-meaning group holds verbs of change with a narrower or broader reach.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 alter 一族以及整条借入的短语；近义组收范围宽窄不一的「变化」类动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a change made to something, especially to a garment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改动、修改」，尤指对衣物的修改。

entries.definition: Able to be changed; the opposite of fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可改变的」，与「固定的」相对。

entries.definition: A second self or a trusted other personality, borrowed whole from Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「另一个自我、第二人格」，整条从拉丁语借入。

entries.definition: Not changed at all, still in the original state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未改变的、原样的」。

entries.definition: The general verb for becoming or making different; broader and far more common than alter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变、变化」，是最一般的说法，比 alter 更宽也更常用。

entries.definition: To change something slightly, usually to improve it or make it suitable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改、调整」，通常指小幅改动以改进或使其适用。

entries.definition: To change a text, law or agreement in order to correct or improve it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修订、修正」，多用于文本、法律或协议。

entries.definition: To change something slightly so that it fits or works better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整」，指小幅改动以更合适或更好用。

entries.definition: To change or differ, especially in amount or degree over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、使有差异」，多指数量或程度随时间变动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin sense of alter and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用 alter 真实的拉丁语本义，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Latin alter means the other of two: to alter is to turn a thing into that other version.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」：alter 就是把东西变成那另一个版本。

normal.en: Alter ego is literally other I, the same alter followed by a different noun.
normal.cn: alter ego 字面就是「另一个我」，用的正是同一个 alter 加另一个名词。

normal.en: A tailor alters clothes: the cloth stays, only its shape becomes other.
normal.cn: 裁缝 alter 衣服：布料不变，只有形状变成另一个样子。

normal.en: Unaltered and alteration keep the same root, one with a negative prefix and one with a noun ending.
normal.cn: unaltered 与 alteration 都保留同一词根，一个加否定前缀，一个加名词词尾。

normal.en: Alter is more formal than change and usually takes a direct object.
normal.cn: alter 比 change 更正式，而且通常直接带宾语。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror showing the same coat with a different cut: one cloth, two shapes.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子照出同一件大衣的另一种剪裁：布只有一块，形状却有两个。

abstract.en: Alter is a small turn of the same object, not a swap for a new one.
abstract.cn: alter 是同一件东西的小幅转向，而不是换成一件新的。

abstract.en: The other of two is the whole idea: first there is a thing, then its other version.
abstract.cn: 「两者中的另一个」就是全部意思：先有一样东西，再有它的另一个版本。

examples.en: A few small repairs would alter the look of the room without much cost.
examples.cn: 几处小修补就能改变房间的样子，花费并不多。

examples.en: The dress was altered twice before the wedding.
examples.cn: 这条裙子在婚礼前改了两次。

examples.en: His public manner is calm, but his alter ego on stage is wild.
examples.cn: 他在人前举止平静，舞台上的另一个自我却很狂放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特」——奥特曼换了个形态，还是同一个，只是变成另一个样子：改变

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」来自原始印欧语 *h₂el-「在……之外、另一个」（重构形式）；加动词词尾 -are 成 alterare「使不同、改变」，经古法语 alterer 进入英语。alter ego 是十六世纪整条借入的拉丁语短语。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of alter all start from the other of two: changing a thing, adjusting a garment, changing by itself, a second self, and a neutered animal.
sensesIntro.cn: alter 的五个义项都从「两者中的另一个」出发：改变事物、改衣、自身变化、另一个自我，以及给动物绝育。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tailor's chalk line redraws an old coat into another shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁缝的粉线在旧大衣上重新划过，把它改成另一个样子。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: an outside hand makes a thing into another version of itself.
branches.cn: 对象线：外来的手把一样东西变成它自己的另一个版本。

branches.en: THE GARMENT: cloth is refitted, so the change is physical and small.
branches.cn: 衣物线：布料被重新剪裁，改动具体而幅度有限。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: without an object, the same change happens inside the thing itself.
branches.cn: 主体线：不带宾语时，同样的变化发生在事物自身之内。

branches.en: THE SECOND SELF: alter ego keeps the Latin phrase and its logic of a pair.
branches.cn: 第二自我线：alter ego 保留拉丁原语，也保留「成对」的逻辑。

branches.en: THE BODY: an animal is made into a non-breeding body, the furthest reach of the same idea.
branches.cn: 身体线：动物被改成不再繁殖的身体，是同一想法延伸得最远的一端。

intro.en: Alter is a Latin comparative word rather than a prefix; the English family is built with ordinary Latin and English endings.
intro.cn: alter 是拉丁语的比较级形式，并不是前缀；英语这一族词靠普通的拉丁语与英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin alter, alius, alterare and alteratio are all recorded, so only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alter、alius、alterare、alteratio 都有文献记录，只有印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The base carries the idea of a second version.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基承载「另一个版本」的意思。

items.example: The ending is generally analysed as making alter a comparative form.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为这个词尾使 alter 成为比较级形式。

items.example: It forms alter ego, a second self.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alter ego，即另一个自我。

latinEntries.meaning: other, another of more than two
latinEntries.meaningCN: 别的；两者以上之中的另一个

definition_zh: 倾向；趋势；癖性
definition_en: a leaning or inclination toward a particular kind of behaviour, direction or outcome
core_image: 一枚小球放在微微倾斜的桌面上，手一松，它总是往同一个方向滚
scene: 议事厅里，同一批人每次表决都往同一个方向靠，连反对者也渐渐跟着举手。 There was a clear tendency for the committee to side with the older members.
sceneCN: 这里本词指群体在反复选择中表现出的固定偏向（第 1 个义项：一般倾向）；句意为委员会明显倾向于站在年长成员一边。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

senses.title: A general leaning
senses.definition: a general leaning of people or things toward one kind of behaviour or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物总体上偏向某一类行为或结果的态势
senses.example: There is a general tendency for prices to rise before holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 节前价格上涨存在一种普遍倾向。
senses.why: The word began as a stretched direction, and the first sense is that leaning seen in a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指被拉伸的方向，第一个义项就是整个群体表现出的这种偏向。

senses.title: A personal habit of mind
senses.definition: a person's habitual inclination to act or feel in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在行为或感受上习惯性的偏向
senses.example: She has a tendency to interrupt when she is nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她紧张时有打断别人的癖性。
senses.why: A single person also leans one way again and again, and the word names that private tilt.
senses.whyCN: 单个人也会一次次往同一侧倾，本词就指这种私人的偏向。

senses.title: A statistical movement
senses.definition: the direction in which a set of figures moves over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据在一段时间内变动的方向
senses.example: The figures show an upward tendency in household savings.
senses.exampleCN: 数据显示家庭储蓄呈上升趋势。
senses.why: Numbers plotted over time lean visibly, and that lean is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按时间画出的数据会显出倾斜，本词描述的正是这种倾斜。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a broad drift of opinion or policy in a society at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期社会舆论或政策上广泛出现的走向
senses.example: A reformist tendency gained ground among younger voters.
senses.exampleCN: 改革倾向在年轻选民中占了上风。
senses.why: When many minds lean together, the lean becomes a public current rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的心思同时倾斜，这种倾斜就成了公共潮流而非私人情绪。

senses.title: A physical drift
senses.definition: the direction in which a body or substance naturally moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 物体或物质自然移动或变化的方向
senses.example: Hot air has a tendency to rise above cooler air.
senses.exampleCN: 热空气有升到冷空气之上的趋向。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical: something stretched or pulled toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理性的：某物被拉向某一点。

senses.title: A medical susceptibility
senses.definition: a bodily weakness that makes a person likely to develop a particular illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上的弱点使人容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: The condition runs in families with a tendency to low bone density.
senses.exampleCN: 该病多见于有骨密度偏低易感性的家族。
senses.why: A body leaning toward illness is described with the same word as any other lean.
senses.whyCN: 身体向疾病倾斜，用的仍是与其它倾斜相同的词。

senses.title: A stylistic leaning in art
senses.definition: a recurring preference for certain forms or moods in an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家作品中反复出现的对某些形式或情绪的偏好
senses.example: His later novels show a tendency toward long, quiet scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 他后期的小说显出偏爱篇幅长而安静的场景。
senses.why: Style is a repeated lean of the hand, and critics borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 风格是手反复倾斜的结果，评论者便借用这个词来指它。

senses.title: A market drift
senses.definition: the direction in which prices or demand appear to be heading
senses.definitionCN: 价格或需求看起来正在走向的方向
senses.example: Traders watched the tendency of the index for the week.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员盯着这一周指数的走势。
senses.why: Markets are read as leaning one way, so forecasters speak of a tendency rather than a certainty.
senses.whyCN: 市场被看作正在往一侧倾，故预测者说倾向而不说定论。

intro.en: Tendency comes from the Latin verb for stretching or aiming, through a medieval Latin noun for a leaning; it is not related to the word for a trend, which comes from an Old English verb for turning.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，经中世纪拉丁语表「倾斜」的名词进入英语；它与表「走势」的那个词并不同源，后者出自古英语中表「转动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to stretch out, hold out or aim, and the image is a body or a line extended toward a point.
items.cn: 这一拉丁动词意为「伸出、朝向、瞄准」，意象是身体或线条朝某一点展开。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed a noun from the participle of that verb, naming a leaning or an inclination.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用该动词的分词造出名词，指倾斜或倾向。

items.en: English took the noun in the seventeenth century for a leaning of mind, body or fortune.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该名词，指心思、身体或运势上的偏向。

items.en: The word for a trend is not a relative: it comes from an Old English verb meaning to turn or revolve, and only later came to mean a direction.
items.cn: 表「走势」的那个词并非同族：它出自古英语中表「转动、旋转」的动词，后来才引申为方向。

items.en: Source uncertain: the older shape of the Latin verb is generally reconstructed, and the first English citation of the noun is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁动词的更早形态一般为重构，该名词在英语中的最早书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close to this noun; group two collects words for leanings of mind or body.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是表示心思或身体偏向的词。

entries.definition: A true relative: the verb means to be inclined or to take care of, and the noun adds a suffix of state.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源：动词表示趋向或照管，名词则加上表状态的后缀。

entries.definition: It means pushing a one-sided view, built on the same leaning root with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 意为推行片面观点，由同一表「倾斜」的词根加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Often treated as a synonym but a different word: it comes from an Old English verb for turning, not from the Latin verb for stretching, so the two are not cognate.
entries.definitionCN: 常被当作同义词，其实是另一个词：它出自古英语表「转动」的动词，而非拉丁语表「伸展」的动词，二者并无同源关系。

entries.definition: It sounds almost the same but comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, and it names the right to occupy property rather than a leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，却出自拉丁语表「握持」的动词，指占用房产的权利，与偏向无关。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind or body, closer to a settled preference than to a measured direction in figures.
entries.definitionCN: 心思或身体上的倾斜，更接近固定的偏好，而非数据中被测量的方向。

entries.definition: A strong natural tendency to behave in a particular way, usually toward something undesirable.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈而天生的行为偏向，通常指向不受欢迎的事。

entries.definition: A person's habitual temperament, the whole cast of mind rather than one lean.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人习惯的性情，是整个心性而非单一偏向。

entries.definition: A slow general movement or change of opinion, stressing gradual motion rather than a built-in lean.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的整体移动或舆论变化，强调渐进，而非内在的倾斜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch: a line pulled toward a point, and that is the image of the whole family.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为伸展：一条被拉向某点的线，这就是整个词族的意象。

normal.en: The family runs tendency, tend, tendentious, tendentiously, tendentiousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括倾向、趋向、有偏向的、带有偏向地与偏向性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a tendency to overreact, a downward tendency, a growing tendency.
normal.cn: 固定说法：过度反应的倾向、下降趋势、日益增长的趋势。

normal.en: Keep it apart from the word for a trend: that one came from an old verb for turning, not from stretching.
normal.cn: 要与表「走势」的那个词分开：后者出自表「转动」的古动词，并非出自「伸展」。

normal.en: Statistics speak of a tendency when a line on a chart slants; medicine speaks of one when a body is likely to fall ill.
normal.cn: 统计学说倾向，是指图表上的线出现斜度；医学说倾向，是指身体容易生病。

abstract.en: Picture a metal ball rolling toward the low edge of a tilted table, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗金属球一次次滚向倾斜桌面的低边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one side of a square without anyone giving an order.
abstract.cn: 想象人群没有接到任何指令，却慢慢移向广场的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that always reaches for the same pen, even when another lies closer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手总去拿同一支笔，哪怕另一支离得更近。

examples.en: Prices show a tendency to fall after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收成之后价格显出下跌的倾向。

examples.en: He has a tendency to talk over people in meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会上有抢别人话头的癖性。

examples.en: The survey found a tendency toward smaller households.
examples.cn: 调查发现家庭规模有变小的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「伸展」记成一条被拉向某处的线：线往哪边斜，就是往哪边倾向。

root: 来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，中世纪拉丁语由其分词构成表「倾斜」的名词，英语借入后指各种偏向；与表「走势」的词不同源，后者出自古英语表「转动」的动词；更深来源一般为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a line or a body stretched toward one point, so that it leans the same way each time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条线或一具身体被拉向某一点，于是每次都往同一侧倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a tilted table, always rolling to the same low corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾斜桌面上的球，总滚向同一个低角。

branches.en: LEANING LINE: the general lean of people and the physical drift of matter share one image of a stretched line.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线：人群的整体偏向与物质的物理趋向共享「被拉长的线」这一意象。

branches.en: PRIVATE LEAN: one person's repeated tilt becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 私人偏向：一个人反复的倾斜成为心理习性。

branches.en: MEASURED SLANT: charts and markets are read as leaning, so the word names a direction in figures.
branches.cn: 可测的斜度：图表与市场都被读作倾斜，本词于是指数据中的方向。

branches.en: PUBLIC CURRENT: many minds leaning together become a drift of opinion.
branches.cn: 公共潮流：许多心思同时倾斜，便成舆论走向。

branches.en: BODY AND ART: a body likely to fall ill and a hand that prefers certain forms both lean in the same old sense.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术：易患病的身体与偏爱某些形式的手，都在同一古老意义上倾斜。

intro.en: The noun is built from a Latin verb and a suffix of state, and English keeps a small family around it, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语动词加表状态的后缀构成，英语周围还保留少量同族词，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb supplies the stretching, the Latin participle supplies the leaning, and English supplies only the closing noun suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词提供「伸展」，拉丁语分词提供「倾斜」，英语只提供收尾的名词后缀。

items.example: The root shows in extend, intend and tension, all about stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于延伸、打算、张力等词，都与伸展有关。

items.example: A bowstring is stretched, and so is a plan toward its aim.
items.exampleCN: 弓弦被拉紧，计划也朝目标伸展。

items.example: The participle describes what is already leaning.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词描述已经在倾斜的东西。

items.structure: tendens plus a medieval Latin noun suffix
items.example: The medieval noun turned the act of leaning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪名词把倾斜这一动作变成一种事物。

items.meaning: a leaning toward a kind of act or outcome
items.example: A tendency can be measured over many cases.
items.exampleCN: 倾向可以在许多个案上被测量出来。

items.example: The report was tendentious from its first line.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告从第一行起就带有偏向。

items.meaning: the quality of pushing a lean
items.example: Readers objected to the tendentiousness of the piece.
items.exampleCN: 读者反对这篇文章的偏向性。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root tend-
items.example: They extended the deadline by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把截止期限延长了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch, to extend, to aim

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上；（古）慷慨地
definition_en: mainly or for the most part, and to a great extent; an older sense of generously survives in literary use
core_image: 天平的一端压得很低，说明几乎所有重量都落在这一边
scene: 统计报告发布后，记者们围在发言人身边提问。 The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
sceneCN: 这里 largely 指「大部分地、主要地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为结果被宣读时人群大体上保持沉默。图中可辨识物件：发布台、话筒、记者的笔记本。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上

derivatives.zh: largely 的原级，源自拉丁语 largus，义为「大的；大量的」
由 large 加 -ness 构成，义为「巨大；宽广」
由 en- 加 large 构成，义为「扩大；放大」

senses.title: Mainly, for the most part
senses.definition: in the main, so that most of something is true or affected
senses.definitionCN: 总体上，指某事物的大部分为真或大部分受到影响
senses.example: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。
senses.why: The adverb grew from a word for abundance, so largely counts the greater part of a whole rather than measuring one point on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自表示「充裕」的词，所以 largely 数的是整体的较大部分，而不是在刻度上量某一点。

senses.title: To a great extent
senses.definition: to a high degree, so that something is greatly influenced or explained by a cause
senses.definitionCN: 达到很高的程度，指某事很大程度上受某原因影响或由它解释
senses.example: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。
senses.why: If most of a result comes from one source, that source acts to a great extent, which is how the proportion sense turns into a degree sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个结果大部分来自某一个来源，这个来源就起了很大的作用，于是「比例」义自然转成「程度」义。

senses.title: Generously, in abundance
senses.definition: in a generous or plentiful way, an older literary sense still found in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 以慷慨或丰足的方式，是旧时文学中仍可见到的较早义项
senses.example: The old lord gave largely to the poor of his village.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老领主对村里的穷人施舍很慷慨。
senses.why: Latin largus meant generous as well as abundant, and the earliest English adverb kept that open hand before the sense narrowed to mainly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 largus 既指充裕也指慷慨，最早的英语副词保留了那只张开的手，后来词义才收窄为「主要地」。

intro.en: Largely is the adverb of large, whose Latin source meant generous and abundant before French gave it the sense of broad.
intro.cn: largely 是 large 的副词形式；large 的拉丁来源本指慷慨、充裕，后来法语才赋予它「宽广」的意思。

items.en: Largus meant abundant, generous and free in giving, with little idea of physical size at first.
items.cn: largus 意为充裕、慷慨、乐于给予，起初几乎不含物理大小的意思。

items.en: Old French large kept the Latin word and added the sense of wide or broad, so size entered the meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 large 承接拉丁词义，又加上「宽、阔」的意思，于是大小进入了词义。

items.en: Middle English large covered both generosity and breadth, and the adverb largely was built with -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语 large 同时含慷慨与宽广，副词 largely 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Largely first meant in a generous or plentiful manner, then drifted towards for the greater part.
items.cn: largely 最初意为「慷慨地、大量地」，后来转向「大部分地」。

items.en: Modern English uses largely almost only for mainly or to a great extent, while the generous sense survives in literary or older use.
items.cn: 现代英语的 largely 几乎只表示「主要地、在很大程度上」，慷慨义只留在文学或较早用法中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the large family and its adverbs; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of proportion.
note.cn: 形近组收 large 一词族及其副词；近义组收其他表示比例的副词。

entries.definition: Big in size or amount, the adjective behind largely.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量大的，是 largely 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something bigger.
The quality of being large.
For the most part, more than anything else.
Usually or in most cases.
Mainly, above all other things.
Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛地；在许多地方或许多人中。

normalIntro.en: The adverb counts the bigger part of a whole, and its Latin root still remembers generosity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词数的是整体中较大的那一部分，它的拉丁词根还记着「慷慨」。

normal.en: Large comes from Latin largus, which meant generous and plentiful before it meant big.
normal.cn: large 来自拉丁语 largus，在表示「大」之前，它先表示慷慨、丰足。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get an adverb that says most of the whole is on one side.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly 得到的副词，意思是整体的大部分都落在一边。

normal.en: Largely because marks the main cause, not the only cause.
normal.cn: largely because 标出主要原因，而不是唯一原因。

normal.en: Largely ignored means ignored by most people, while largely unchanged means changed only a little.
normal.cn: largely ignored 指被大多数人忽视；largely unchanged 指只改变了一点点。

normal.en: The generous sense survives in older writing, where giving largely means giving freely.
normal.cn: 慷慨义留在较早的文字里，giving largely 就是慷慨地给予。

abstract.en: A word for an open hand became a word for the bigger share: abundance turns into proportion.
abstract.cn: 一个形容张开的手的词变成了「较大份额」的词：充裕转成了比例。

abstract.en: To say largely is to leave a small door open, because most is not all.
abstract.cn: 说 largely 就是留一扇小门，因为「大部分」并不等于全部。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a crowd as one body, not as a hundred separate opinions.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把人群当成一个整体来衡量，而不是一百个各自独立的意见。

examples.en: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。

examples.en: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
examples.cn: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。

examples.en: The village is now largely deserted in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子在冬天如今大都空着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉直了」——把大部分道理拉直说明白；谐音记住 largely 是主要地。

root: 由 large 加 -ly 构成；large 源自拉丁语 largus（充裕、慷慨），经古法语 large（宽、大）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the greater part of a whole; the word then measures degree, and an older sense of generous giving survives at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是整体中的较大部分；词义由此转为衡量程度，而「慷慨给予」的旧义留在边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with almost all the weight settled on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上几乎所有重量都压在一边。

branches.en: a mostly silent hall during an announcement
branches.cn: 宣布结果时大体安静的大厅

branches.en: a region that is mostly farmland
branches.cn: 大部分是农田的地区

branches.en: a success explained by one strong cause
branches.cn: 由一个强原因解释的成功

branches.en: a report left almost untouched
branches.cn: 几乎原封未动的报告

branches.en: an old lord giving freely to the poor
branches.cn: 老领主慷慨施舍穷人

intro.en: The word is an adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the adjective itself comes from a Latin word for plenty.
intro.cn: 这个词是形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly，而形容词本身来自一个表示「丰足」的拉丁词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 地点；斑点；发现；玷污；（名）现场；_spotlight 聚光
definition_en: a particular place, or a small round mark, or to notice something
core_image: 一盏舞台聚光灯在地板上打出一圈亮斑，光点正好落在主角脚下
scene: 剧场后台，场记板咔哒一响。 The director spotted the young actor in the crowd of extras.
sceneCN: 这里 spot 是「发现、认出」（第 3 个义项：从人群中辨认出）；句意为导演在群众演员中发现了那位年轻演员。图中可辨识物件：场记板、聚光灯、人群。

pos.zh: 名词：地点；斑点；现场；聚光灯（the spot）

derivatives.zh: 复合词，义为「聚光灯；公众注目」
过去分词作形容词，义为「有斑点的」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「一尘不染的」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「观察员；瞄准手」

senses.title: A particular place or location
senses.definition: a particular place or point on a surface or in an area
senses.definitionCN: 表面上或区域内的某个确定位置
senses.example: This is the exact spot where the old bridge stood.
senses.exampleCN: 这就是老桥当年所在的确切地点。
senses.why: A mark pins one place out of all others: the eye points where the dot sits.
senses.whyCN: 一个标记把某处从万处中钉出：眼睛指往圆点所在。

senses.title: A small round mark
senses.definition: a small round mark of a different colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色不同的小圆点
senses.example: The leopard's coat is covered in dark spots.
senses.exampleCN: 豹的皮毛布满深色斑点。
senses.why: The dot is the smallest visible thing: everything larger is made of places.
senses.whyCN: 圆点是最小的可见物：更大的都由「位置」拼成。

senses.title: To notice or catch sight of
senses.definition: to notice someone or something, especially suddenly or with difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 注意到人或物，尤指突然或费劲地
senses.example: She spotted her old teacher across the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市场那头认出了老老师。
senses.why: The mark inside the eye: one detail stands out from the field.
senses.whyCN: 眼中的「斑点」：一个细节从背景里凸出来。

senses.title: To stain or dirty something
senses.definition: to mark or stain something with small patches
senses.definitionCN: 以小块污迹弄脏某物
senses.example: Coffee spotted the white tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在白桌布上留下斑点。
senses.why: The dot falls where it will, and cleanliness is its victim.
senses.whyCN: 圆点随意落下，洁净成了受害者。

senses.title: On the spot: immediately or in trouble
senses.titleCN: on the spot：当场；为难境地
senses.definition: immediately, or in a difficult position requiring instant decision
senses.definitionCN: 立刻，或处于需即刻决断的困境
senses.example: The paramedics treated him on the spot.
senses.exampleCN: 急救员当场为他救治。
senses.why: The pointed place is where pressure lands: here and now.
senses.whyCN: 被钉住的点正是压力落处：就在此时此地。

senses.title: The spotlight and public attention
senses.definition: public attention or prominence, as in the spotlight
senses.definitionCN: 公众的注目，如聚光灯之下
senses.example: The scandal kept the minister in the spotlight.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻让部长一直处于聚光灯下。
senses.why: The stage mark of light picks one body for every eye.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上的光斑为每双眼睛挑出一个身影。

senses.title: A weak spot: a point of failure
senses.definition: a point where something or someone is vulnerable
senses.definitionCN: 事物或人易受攻击之处
senses.example: The plan's weak spot was its transport schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的弱点在运输时间表。
senses.why: Where the dot sits, the surface can be pierced.
senses.whyCN: 圆点所在之处，表面可被穿透。

senses.title: A spot of: a small amount
senses.definition: a small amount of something, especially tea or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 少量某物，尤指茶或麻烦
senses.example: Let us have a spot of tea before we go.
senses.exampleCN: 走之前我们喝点茶吧。
senses.why: The dot shrinks the whole pot to a single mark of it.
senses.whyCN: 圆点把整壶缩成一个小小的标记。

intro.en: Spot is a native word of the mark and the dot, with a scattered family across the northern seas.
intro.cn: spot 是「标记与圆点」的本土词，词族散布在北方海域。

items.en: *spitt- is generally reconstructed as "to splash, speck"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spitt- 表示「溅上、斑点」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse spotti meant "a small spot or speck", the accepted near relative.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 spotti 意为「小斑点」，是公认的近亲。

items.en: Middle English spotte meant a stain or small mark, also a moral stain.
items.cn: 中古英语 spotte 指污渍或小点，也指道德污点。

items.en: The place sense grew from the marked point on a map or surface.
items.cn: 「地点」义由表面上被标记的点发展而来。

items.en: The word now serves maps, stains, eyes, spotlights and instant decisions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于地图、污渍、眼睛、聚光灯与当机立断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for marks and places.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收表示标记与地点的词。

entries.definition: A lamp that lights one area, or public attention.
Covered in marks, as a spotted dog.
Completely clean, without a single mark.
A quarrel or past of spit; letters shuffled and of different line.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「争吵」或 spit 的过去式；字母换位，词系不同。

entries.definition: Games and contests; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「运动」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: A general word for where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「某物所在」的通用词。

entries.definition: A mark that sinks in and is hard to remove.
A very tiny spot or particle.
To become aware of something.
A spot of ink or a moral stain.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dot image and the idioms the word really carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用圆点意象与该词的真实习语。

normal.en: A spot is a dot: a mark that also marks a place.
normal.cn: spot 是圆点：既作标记也标地点。

normal.en: On the spot means right there, right now.
normal.cn: on the spot 意为就在现场、就在此刻。

normal.en: Spot on means the answer hit the exact point.
normal.cn: spot on 表示答案正中靶点。

normal.en: Put on the spot is being pressed to answer at once.
normal.cn: put on the spot 是被当场逼问。

normal.en: A spot check samples a few random points.
normal.cn: spot check 从随机几个点抽样。

abstract.en: Picture the spotlight's circle on the floorboards: one bright dot among dark ones.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯在地板上的圆圈：暗色中的一点亮斑。

abstract.en: The eye is a hunter of dots: one fleck moving, and it is caught.
abstract.cn: 眼睛是圆点猎人：一点异动即被捕获。

abstract.en: Where the dot lands, the story happens: place and mark are one.
abstract.cn: 圆点落于何处，故事便发生何处：地点与标记合一。

examples.en: The hiker chose a shady spot for the lunch break.
examples.cn: 徒步者选了一处阴凉地点午餐歇脚。

examples.en: The doctor spotted the tiny rash behind the ear at once.
examples.cn: 医生立刻发现了耳后的细小皮疹。

examples.en: Rain spotted the window and blurred the street outside.
examples.cn: 雨点打上窗户，模糊了外面的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯波特」——聚光圈钉住一点：地点；斑点；发现

root: spot 属日耳曼语源，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spitt- 表示「溅上、斑点」，与古诺斯语 spotti「小斑点」相关，更早来源不确定。中古英语 spotte 兼指污渍与道德污点，「地点」义后起。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spot all circle one dot: the mark, the place it pins, the eye that finds it, and the stain that spoils.
sensesIntro.cn: spot 的义项都围绕一个圆点：标记、它钉住的地点、找到它的眼睛与弄脏它的污迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of spotlight on dark floorboards.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗色地板上聚光灯的一圈亮斑。

branches.en: THE MARK LINE: the dot on the map and the fleck on the coat.
branches.cn: 标记线：地图上的点与皮毛上的斑。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: one detail stands out and is caught.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：一个细节凸出并被捕获。

branches.en: THE STAIN LINE: where the dot falls, the surface can fail.
branches.cn: 污渍线：圆点落处，表面可破。

branches.en: THE HERE-AND-NOW LINE: decisions taken on the spot, troubles in small doses.
branches.cn: 此地此刻线：当场决断，麻烦按小份来。

branches.en: THE LIGHT LINE: the marked point becomes the stage's circle.
branches.cn: 光斑线：被标记的点化作舞台的圆。

intro.en: Spot is a bare Germanic root; compounds and suffixes gather around the dot.
intro.cn: spot 是裸的日耳曼词根；复合词与后缀围绕圆点聚集。

latinIntro.en: Spot is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spot 属日耳曼语源，拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: It is the nearest recorded relative.
The phrase pins time and place together.
items.exampleCN: 该短语把时间与地点钉在一起。

items.example: The phrase hits the marked point.
items.exampleCN: 该短语正中被标记的点。

由本词加后缀构成，义为「一尘不染的」
