definition_zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上
definition_en: by a large amount or degree
core_image: 水位一夜之间涨到台阶的第三级
scene: 一夜大雨之后，河里的水位明显升高。 The road became considerably more dangerous after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 considerably 指「相当大地」（第 1 个义项：程度很大地）；句意是天黑之后这条路变得危险多了。

pos.zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上

derivatives.zh: 相当大的；相当多的
考虑；认为
考虑；体谅
体贴的

senses.title: To a large degree
senses.definition: by a large amount or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上很大地
senses.example: The cost rose considerably last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年的成本大幅上涨。
senses.why: The change is too big to be waved away as small.
senses.whyCN: 这个变化太大，不能当作小事挥开。

senses.title: Before comparatives
senses.definition: used with more or a comparative to mean much
senses.definitionCN: 与 more 或比较级连用，表示…得多
senses.example: The new engine is considerably quieter.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机安静得多。
senses.why: A comparison needs a weight word to show the gap is wide.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要一个表示分量的词，说明差距很大。

senses.title: In a notable way
senses.definition: in a way that is easy to notice
senses.definitionCN: 以容易被人察觉的方式
senses.example: Her accent changed considerably over the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这一年里她的口音变化很明显。
senses.why: Some changes announce themselves before you measure them.
senses.whyCN: 有些变化在你测量之前就先自己报了名。

intro.en: Considerably is considerable plus -ly, from Latin considerare, to examine closely.
intro.cn: considerably 是 considerable 加 -ly，源头是拉丁语 considerare，意为仔细审视。

items.en: Considerare meant to look at something with care.
items.cn: considerare 意为带着留心去看某物。

items.en: The adjective considerabilis meant worth noticing.
items.cn: 形容词 considerabilis 意为值得注意的。

items.en: English considerable first meant able to be considered.
items.cn: 英语 considerable 最初指可以被考虑的。

items.en: The sense shifted toward large in size or amount.
items.cn: 它的含义转向规模或数量很大。

items.en: The adverb considerably grew common with comparatives.
items.cn: 副词 considerably 开始常与比较级连用。

items.en: It now simply strengthens how large a change is.
items.cn: 如今它只是加强说明变化有多大。

note.en: The look-alike group is the consider family, and the meaning group names other adverbs of large degree.
note.cn: 形近组是 consider 家族，近义组列出其他表示程度大的副词。

entries.definition: large enough to be noticed
thoughtful about other people
careful thought about something
very much
in a way large enough to matter
to a large and solid degree
entries.definitionCN: 达到很大而实在的程度

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a river that climbed the steps, then move to a quieter engine and to an accent that changed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从涨上台阶的河水开始，再到更安静的发动机，最后到变了样的口音。

normal.en: Considerably is considerable turned into an adverb: in a big way.
normal.cn: considerably 是 considerable 的副词，意思是以很大的方式。

normal.en: It almost always leans on a comparative: more, better, higher.
normal.cn: 它几乎总靠在比较级上：more、better、higher。

normal.en: A considerably higher price is one you feel before you calculate.
normal.cn: 高出不少的价格，你在算之前就先感觉到了。

normal.en: If the change needs a photo to prove it, it is considerable.
normal.cn: 若这变化需要照片才能证明，那就算相当大了。

normal.en: One word adds weight to the scale of any sentence.
normal.cn: 一个词，就能给任何句子的天平加砝码。

abstract.en: Picture water touching the third step of a stair.
abstract.cn: 想象水漫到楼梯的第三级。

abstract.en: Picture two lines on a graph pulling far apart.
abstract.cn: 想象图上两条线越拉越开。

abstract.en: Picture a needle moving well past the middle mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针远远越过中间那条刻度。

examples.en: The road became considerably more dangerous after dark.
examples.cn: 天黑之后这条路变得危险多了。

examples.en: Prices have risen considerably this year.
examples.cn: 今年物价大幅上涨。

examples.en: Her writing improved considerably after the course.
examples.cn: 上完这门课之后，她的写作进步很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 considerably 记成 considerable（相当大的）加 ly：用相当大的幅度去做某件事，就是相当大地。

root: 由拉丁语 considerare（审视）经 considerable 加 -ly 构成，表示程度或数量上很大的方式。

sensesIntro.en: From a plain large degree, to its usual place before comparatives, and finally to a change anyone can see.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯表示程度大，到常站在比较级前面，最后到人人都看得见的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle pushed well past the middle mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针被推过中间刻度很远。

branches.en: The main sense is a large degree of change.
branches.cn: 主要义项是变化程度很大。

branches.en: Before a comparative it marks a wide gap.
branches.cn: 放在比较级前面时，它标出很大的差距。

branches.en: The third sense stresses that the change is visible.
branches.cn: 第三个义项强调这种变化看得见。

branches.en: The adverb either stands alone or leans on a comparison.
branches.cn: 这个副词要么单独站着，要么靠在比较上。

branches.en: A gap wide enough to see is a gap worth the word.
branches.cn: 宽到看得见的差距，才配得上这个词。

intro.en: Considerably is considerable plus -ly, from Latin considerare, to examine.
intro.cn: considerably 是 considerable 加 -ly，源自拉丁语 considerare（审视）。

latinIntro.en: The star base sider- also appears in sidereal, and desire shares the same old root.
latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，desire 也共享同一个古老词根。

items.exampleCN: 随后出现了相当长的延误。
把两个答案都考虑一下。

items.example: Sidereal time drifts from clock time.
items.exampleCN: 恒星时与钟表时间会错开。

definition_zh: 走廊；过道；狭长地带
definition_en: a long narrow passage inside a building, or a narrow strip of land between two areas
core_image: 一条长长的通道，两侧的门一扇接一扇，尽头透进白光
scene: 医院三楼的走廊很长，尽头那扇窗透进一片白光。 A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 corridor 指「走廊」（第 1 个义项：建筑物内连接房间的长通道）；句意是一位护士快步走过走廊。

collocations.phrase: at the end of the corridor

derivatives.zh: 信使；快递员（与 corridor 同源于「跑」）
路线；进程（同源词）
光标（同源词，本指奔跑者）

senses.title: A passage inside a building
senses.definition: a long narrow passage that connects rooms in a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物内连接各个房间的狭长通道
senses.example: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一位护士快步走过走廊。
senses.why: A building needs a spine so that its rooms can be one body.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一根脊梁，房间才能连成一个身体。

senses.title: A strip of land
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长土地
senses.example: The road runs through a narrow corridor of land.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过一条狭长地带。
senses.why: Countries also need passages, and they guard them like doors.
senses.whyCN: 国家也需要通道，并像守门一样守着它们。

senses.title: The aisle of a train
senses.definition: the narrow walking space between seats in a train or plane
senses.definitionCN: 火车或飞机座位之间供人行走的窄道
senses.example: He stood in the corridor with his ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿着车票站在车厢过道里。
senses.why: Even a moving box needs a line along which people pass.
senses.whyCN: 即使是一只移动的盒子，也需要一条让人通过的线。

intro.en: Corridor comes from Italian corridore, a runner or running place, from correre, to run, and Latin currere.
intro.cn: corridor 来自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），源自 correre（跑）与拉丁语 currere。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为奔跑。

items.en: Corridore named a runner or a place for running.
items.cn: corridore 指奔跑的人或供奔跑的地方。

items.en: French corridor named a narrow passage in a fortress.
items.cn: 法语 corridor 指堡垒中的狭窄通道。

items.en: English corridor first meant a covered walk or gallery.
items.cn: 英语 corridor 最初指有顶的步道或长廊。

items.en: It now means any long passage, in a building or on a map.
items.cn: 今天它指任何长通道，无论在大楼里还是地图上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the running base curr-, and the meaning group names other ways through a building.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示奔跑的词基 curr-，近义组列出其他穿过建筑的说法。

entries.definition: to eat away metal slowly
to drive animals into an enclosure
a ring of light around the sun
a passage just inside the front door
a narrow way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处通向另一处的窄道

entries.definition: the space between rows of seats

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long passage lined with doors, then move to a narrow strip of land and to a train aisle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两侧都是门的长通道开始，再到狭长地带，最后到车厢过道。

normal.en: Corridor comes from a word for running, so it is a place made for moving.
normal.cn: corridor 源自表示奔跑的词，所以它是为移动而设的地方。

normal.en: A corridor has two rows of doors and no chairs.
normal.cn: 走廊有两排门，却没有椅子。

normal.en: Hospitals keep corridors long so that beds can pass.
normal.cn: 医院把走廊修得长，是为了让病床通过。

normal.en: A land corridor is a hallway between two countries.
normal.cn: 陆上走廊就是两国之间的一条过道。

normal.en: The double r in the middle keeps the word running.
normal.cn: 中间的两个 r 让这个词一直向前跑。

abstract.en: Picture a line of doors standing one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门一层层排在身后。

abstract.en: Picture a thin neck of land joining two wide rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的陆地，把两片宽阔的土地连起来。

abstract.en: Picture light at the far end of a very long tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条很长隧道的尽头有光。

examples.en: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
examples.cn: 一位护士快步走过走廊。

examples.en: Their office is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 他们的办公室在走廊尽头。

examples.en: The train corridor was full of luggage.
examples.cn: 火车过道里堆满了行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corridor 记成「能跑的道」：两侧是门、中间能一路跑到尽头，就是走廊。

root: 源自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），来自 correre（跑），再上溯到拉丁语 currere（奔跑），本指供人穿行的长道。

sensesIntro.en: From a passage between rooms, to a thin strip of land, and at last to the aisle of a moving carriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间之间的通道，到一条细长的土地，最后到移动车厢里的过道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow passage with doors on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长而窄的通道，两侧都是门。

branches.en: The corridor turns separate rooms into one building.
branches.cn: 走廊把一个个房间变成一栋完整的建筑。

branches.en: A narrow strip of land turns two areas into neighbours.
branches.cn: 一条狭长土地把两片区域变成邻居。

branches.en: An aisle lets people pass while the carriage moves.
branches.cn: 过道让人们在车厢移动时仍能通行。

branches.en: Both are thin lines that join larger spaces.
branches.cn: 两者都是连接较大空间的细线。

branches.en: Land corridor and train aisle are both narrow routes of passage.
branches.cn: 陆上走廊与车厢过道都是狭窄的通行路线。

intro.en: Corridor is built on Latin currere, to run, through Italian corridore, a running place.
intro.cn: corridor 建立在拉丁语 currere（奔跑）之上，经意大利语 corridore（跑道）而来。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- also appears in current, cursor and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 也出现在 current、cursor 与 excursion 中。

items.meaning: a train with a side passage
items.example: The corridor train stops at every town.
items.exampleCN: 这趟走廊式列车逢站就停。

items.meaning: a carriage with a side passage
items.example: We sat in the corridor coach.
items.exampleCN: 我们坐在走廊式车厢里。

items.meaning: a path or direction of movement
water or air that runs forward
a moving mark on a screen

definition_zh: 仔细地；密切地；紧密地
definition_en: in a careful and attentive way, or in a way that is very near or tightly connected
core_image: 放大镜几乎贴到纸面上
scene: 实验室里两个人并肩盯着同一块切片。 The two teams worked closely on the design.
sceneCN: 这里 closely 指「密切地」（第 2 个义项：紧密相连地）；句意是两支团队在设计上密切合作。

derivatives.zh: 近的；亲密的
亲密；接近
关闭的

senses.title: With careful attention
senses.definition: with great attention to detail, so that nothing is missed
senses.definitionCN: 非常注意细节，不遗漏任何东西
senses.example: The doctor looked closely at the small scar.
senses.exampleCN: 医生仔细察看那道小疤痕。
senses.why: To look close means to bring your eyes near, and near looking means careful looking.
senses.whyCN: look close 是把眼睛凑近，凑近了看自然是仔细地看。

senses.title: In a tightly connected way
senses.definition: in a way that is very near or strongly linked
senses.definitionCN: 以非常接近或联系很强的方式
senses.example: The two industries are closely linked.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个行业紧密相连。
senses.why: The adverb simply carries the near sense of the adjective into verbs and participles.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把形容词的「近」义带入动词和分词。

intro.en: Closely is the adjective close plus the old adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: closely 就是形容词 close 加上古老的副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Claudere meant to shut, and its participle meant shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭，其分词意为已关上的。

items.en: Clos meant enclosed and described things packed near.
items.cn: clos 意为围起来的，形容靠得很近的事物。

items.en: The adjective close entered English with the near sense.
items.cn: 形容词 close 带着「近」的含义进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ly turned the adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变为方式副词。

items.en: Closely now covers careful attention as well as physical nearness.
items.cn: closely 如今既指细心关注，也指空间接近。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective and nouns built on the same stem, while the meaning group names careful and tight ways of acting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词与名词，近义组列出仔细与紧密的行事方式。

entries.definition: near in space, time or feeling
entries.definitionCN: 在空间、时间或感情上接近的

entries.definition: the state of being near or intimate
the shutting of a place or a feeling of ending
entries.definitionCN: 场所关闭，或事情了结的感觉

entries.definition: with attention and caution
with strong and fixed attention
entries.definitionCN: 以强烈而专注的注意力

entries.definition: in a firm and secure way

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the adjective behind the adverb, the magnifying glass and the linked chains.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从副词背后的形容词、放大镜和相扣的链条入手。

normal.en: Take the adjective close, add -ly, and the adverb is ready.
normal.cn: 拿形容词 close 加 -ly，副词就成了。

normal.en: Closely related is a fixed pair that appears in almost every academic text.
normal.cn: closely related 是固定搭配，几乎每篇学术文章都能见到。

normal.en: Look closely means bring your face near the page.
normal.cn: look closely 就是把脸凑近纸面。

normal.en: Work closely means the desks are near and the talk is constant.
normal.cn: work closely 意味着桌子挨得近，交流不断。

normal.en: The adverb never changes form, so no plural or tense is needed.
normal.cn: 这个副词从不改变形式，不需要复数或时态。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass almost touching the print.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚放大镜几乎贴到字面上。

abstract.en: Picture two workers leaning over the same drawing.
abstract.cn: 想象两名工人俯身看同一张图纸。

abstract.en: Picture two rings linked so that neither can slip free.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚环相扣，谁都脱不开。

examples.en: Read the contract closely before you sign it.
examples.cn: 签字之前仔细读一遍合同。

examples.en: Diet and mood are closely connected.
examples.cn: 饮食与情绪密切相关。

examples.en: The police are watching the port closely.
examples.cn: 警方正在密切监视这个港口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 closely 记成「贴近地」：贴得近，才看得细，也才连得紧。

root: 由形容词 close 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，close 源自拉丁语 claudere（关闭），引申为围合而接近。

sensesIntro.en: The same adverb covers nearness of the eye and nearness of connection.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词既指眼睛贴近，也指联系紧密。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something brought so near that no gap remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被拉到极近，几乎不留缝隙。

branches.en: Nearness of the eye becomes care in looking.
branches.cn: 眼睛的贴近变成观看时的细心。

branches.en: Nearness between things becomes a strong link.
branches.cn: 事物之间的贴近变成牢固的联系。

branches.en: Both senses come from the adjective close and its idea of no distance.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自形容词 close 及其「没有距离」的意思。

branches.en: The word often pairs with linked, related and tied.
branches.cn: 这个词常与 linked、related、tied 搭配。

branches.en: Care and connection are two readings of one small gap.
branches.cn: 细心与联系是同一个小缝隙的两种读法。

intro.en: The adverb is a suffix product, and its family comes from the adjective close.
intro.cn: 这个副词是加后缀的产物，其家族来自形容词 close。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin claudere, to shut, through French clos, enclosed.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 claudere（关闭），经法语 clos（围起来的）而来。

items.example: The station is close to the hotel.
This path is closer than the road.
She chose the closest seat to the door.
items.exampleCN: 她选了离门最近的座位。

items.example: The closeness of the houses surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 房屋之间挨得之近让他吃惊。

items.meaning: in a near or careful way
items.example: The two issues are closely related.
The office is closed on Sunday.
The closing date is next Friday.

items.meaning: the act of shutting something down
items.example: The closure left the town without a bank.
items.exampleCN: 这次关闭让小镇没有了银行。

latinEntries.example: Clausum gave French clos and English close.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clausum 衍生出法语 clos 与英语 close。

definition_zh: 出生的；本地的；原产的；天生的；（计算机）原生的；本地居民；原住民
definition_en: born in or belonging naturally to a particular place, and hence original or inborn
core_image: 一株只长在这面山坡的野花，根须抓住本地的碎石，移栽到别处便枯死
scene: 这面山坡上只长这一种野花，移栽到别处总活不成。 The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 native 指原产于某地的（第 2 个义项：天然属于某地）；句意为这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。

pos.zh: 出生的；本地的（指生于某地或天然属于某地）
天生的；固有的（指与生俱来的性质）
（计算机）原生的（为某平台原生开发）

derivatives.zh: 原生地；天生地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）
出生；诞生（由拉丁词干加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由「出生的」转指「出生」这一事件）
本地出生的（由基础形容词与表出生的成分复合而成，由「出生」转指「生于本地」的身份）
本族性；母语程度（由基础形容词加表抽象状态的名词后缀而来，由性质转指抽象状态）
民族；国家（由拉丁同一词干加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，同一「出生」词根，由「出生的人群」转指「民族」）

senses.title: Born in a place
senses.definition: having been born in a particular place or country
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地方或国家出生的
senses.example: She is a native of the coastal town and knows every lane.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座海滨小镇本地出生的人，认得每一条小巷。
senses.why: The Latin root is birth itself; the adjective begins as a plain statement about where someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本身就是「出生」；这个形容词起初只是关于出生地的平实陈述。

senses.title: Belonging to a place naturally
senses.definition: growing or living naturally in a region and not introduced from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区自然生长或生活，而非从别处引入的
senses.example: The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。
senses.why: The same birth relation applies to species: a plant is 'born' in its range and does not need a person to place it there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的出生关系也适用于物种：植物在其分布区内「出生」，不需要人把它放到那里。

senses.title: Indigenous person
senses.definition: a member of the peoples who lived in a territory before later settlers
senses.definitionCN: 在后来定居者之前就生活于某片土地的民族的成员
senses.example: The treaty was signed with the native inhabitants, not with the settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 条约是与原住居民签订的，而不是与定居者。
senses.why: The noun turns the birth relation into a political identity, and modern usage often prefers indigenous for this sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把出生关系变成政治身份；现代用法在这一义项上更常用「原住民族」这一说法。

senses.title: Inborn quality
senses.definition: present from birth rather than learned or acquired
senses.definitionCN: 出生时就有、而非习得或获得的
senses.example: He has a native talent for hearing pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 他有分辨音高的天赋。
senses.why: If native means born with a place, it can also mean born with a quality; the metaphor moves from location to nature.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指「生在某地」，它也能指「生来带有某种性质」；这个比喻从地点移到了天性。

senses.title: Unmixed material
senses.definition: found in a pure form in nature, as of metals
senses.definitionCN: 在自然界以纯净形态存在，如某些金属
senses.example: The riverbed holds native copper, not ore.
senses.exampleCN: 河床里有天然铜，而不是矿石。
senses.why: A metal 'native to the earth' is one that nature left uncombined; the sense narrows to chemical purity.
senses.whyCN: 「生在大地之中」的金属，就是自然留下、未经化合的那种；词义收窄到化学纯度。

senses.title: Built for a platform
senses.definition: designed to run directly on a particular operating system or device
senses.definitionCN: 为某一操作系统或设备直接运行而设计的
senses.example: The native app opens faster than the web version.
senses.exampleCN: 原生应用比网页版打开得更快。
senses.why: Computing borrows the word for belonging: software native to a system needs no translator layer.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了「属于」这一含义：属于某系统的软件不需要转译层。

senses.title: First-learned language
senses.definition: the language a person acquired in childhood, often called the mother tongue
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在童年习得的语言，常称为母语
senses.example: Her native language is not the one she writes in now.
senses.exampleCN: 她的母语并不是她现在写作所用的语言。
senses.why: Language is acquired at birth-time, so the adjective marks the earliest layer of speech rather than national origin.
senses.whyCN: 语言在出生时期被习得，因此这个形容词标记言语的最早层次，而非国籍。

senses.title: A local resident
senses.definition: a person who lives in a place by birth rather than by recent arrival
senses.definitionCN: 因出生而居住在某地、而非近期到来的人
senses.example: The shopkeeper is a native but the cook arrived last year.
senses.exampleCN: 店主是本地人，厨师则是去年才来的。
senses.why: In everyday use the noun simply contrasts old residents with newcomers, with no legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这个名词只是把老居民与新来者对照，没有法律分量。

senses.title: The colonial label
senses.definition: the dated and often demeaning use of the noun for colonised peoples
senses.definitionCN: 殖民时代用来指被殖民人群的过时且常含贬抑的名词用法
senses.example: Colonial reports used the noun in a way that modern editors avoid.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民报告使用这个名词的方式，现代编辑会回避。
senses.why: A neutral birth word can be turned into a category of rule; this sense names that history rather than endorsing it.
senses.whyCN: 一个中性的出生词可以被变成统治的类别；这个义项命名那段历史，而非认可它。

intro.en: Native comes from Latin nativus 'innate, born', from nasci 'to be born', whose older form gnasci belongs to the gen- root seen in genus and generate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: native 来自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，源自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式 gnasci 属于 gen- 词根，该词根也见于 genus 与 generate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born, to arise' is a deponent verb; its older form gnasci shows the initial g that survives in cognate words.
items.cn: nasci「出生、产生」是异态动词；其更早形式 gnasci 显示出词首的 g，这个 g 在同族词中保留下来。

items.en: Nativus meant 'innate, natural, born with one', and also 'of birth'. It could describe a person born in a place and a quality present from birth.
items.cn: nativus 意为「天生的、自然的、生来带有的」，也指「出生的」。它既能描述生于某地的人，也能描述与生俱来的性质。

items.en: The gen- root 'to be born, beget' is reconstructed; it also underlies genus, genius, generate and nation. The reconstruction is standard but the exact ablaut grades are reconstructed forms.
items.cn: 表示「出生、生育」的 gen- 词根属重构；它也是 genus、genius、generate 与 nation 的基础。这一重构是通行的，但具体的元音交替形式均属重构。

items.en: Old French natif carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of inborn and later of local birth.
items.cn: 古法语 natif 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，先表示「天生的」，后表示「本地出生的」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun was used by settlers for the peoples they colonised, a usage now recognised as demeaning and largely replaced.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词被定居者用来指他们所殖民的人群；这一用法如今被认定为贬抑性的，且多被取代。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Latin shape of the birth root is a reconstruction, and the date at which the computing sense appeared is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个「出生」词根在拉丁语之前的确切形状属重构形式；计算机义项出现的年代也没有精确固定。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours from the same birth root; group two holds words for original belonging.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「出生」词根的近邻词；第二组表示原初归属。

entries.definition: A people or state, from the same birth root; it names a collectivity, while native names a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 民族或国家，同出「出生」词根；它命名一个集合，而 native 命名一种关系。

entries.definition: Relating to birth, as in natal care; it is medical and temporal, with no sense of belonging to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 与出生有关的，如产后护理；它属医学与时间用法，不含「属于某地」之意。

entries.definition: A birth, especially the Nativity; it names the event rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 出生，尤指耶稣诞生；它命名事件，而非性质。

entries.definition: Lacking experience; it comes from French naive, from Latin nativus 'natural', but developed the sense of unworldly.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏经验的；来自法语 naive，再上溯拉丁 nativus「自然的」，但发展出「不通世故」之义。

entries.definition: Native to a territory before settlers; it is the preferred term in law and advocacy.
entries.definitionCN: 先于定居者而原产于某地；它是法律与倡议中更受青睐的说法。

entries.definition: Of a nearby place; it says nothing about birth or priority.
entries.definitionCN: 属于附近地方的；不涉及出生或时间在先。

entries.definition: Present from birth as a quality; it covers only the innate sense of native.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质与生俱来的；只覆盖 native 的天生义。

entries.definition: Found only in one region, often of species or disease; it stresses restriction rather than birth.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病；强调局限，而非出生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real birth root, its real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「出生」词根、其真实同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Native means born: the same root gives nation, natal and nativity.
normal.cn: native 意为「出生的」：同一词根给出 nation、natal、nativity。

normal.en: A plant native to a slope is 'born' there; a native speaker was 'born into' the language.
normal.cn: 原产山坡的植物是在那里「出生」的；母语者是被「生进」那门语言的。

normal.en: Native copper is metal nature left unmixed, the chemical version of 'belonging to the earth'.
normal.cn: 天然铜是自然留下、未经混合的金属，即「属于大地」的化学版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: native speaker, native species, native to, a native of.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：母语者、本地物种、原产于、本地出生的人。

normal.en: The plural natives is neutral only for local residents; for peoples, indigenous is safer.
normal.cn: 复数 natives 只在指本地居民时中性；指民族时，用 indigenous 更稳妥。

abstract.en: Picture a root system that refuses to hold in foreign gravel.
abstract.cn: 想象一套根须，在陌生的碎石里怎么也抓不住。

abstract.en: Picture a word learned at a kitchen table before any classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在饭桌旁、任何教室之前就学会的词。

abstract.en: Picture software that speaks the machine's own language without an interpreter.
abstract.cn: 想象一种软件，不用翻译就说着机器自己的语言。

examples.en: The eucalyptus is native to Australia but grows all over the world now.
examples.cn: 桉树原产于澳大利亚，如今却长遍世界。

examples.en: A native speaker may still not know why a sentence is grammatical.
examples.cn: 母语者仍可能不知道一个句子为何合乎语法。

examples.en: The app was rebuilt as a native version for each platform.
examples.cn: 这个应用被重做成各平台的原生版本。

senses.title: Something that annoys or troubles
senses.definition: a thing, situation or event that annoys people or causes them trouble
senses.definitionCN: 让人心烦或给人添麻烦的事物、情况或事件
senses.example: The constant buzzing became a nuisance that kept the whole family awake.
senses.exampleCN: 持续不断的嗡嗡声成了搅得全家睡不着的麻烦。
senses.why: Old French nuisance meant harm and annoyance, from a verb for hurting, so the word begins as the discomfort itself rather than the thing causing it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 nuisance 意为「损害、烦扰」，源自表示「伤害」的动词，所以这个词一开始指的就是那份不舒服，而不是造成它的东西。

senses.title: A person who annoys others
senses.titleCN: 讨厌的人；讨人嫌的家伙
senses.definition: a person whose behaviour annoys other people
senses.definitionCN: 行为让别人厌烦的人
senses.example: He made a nuisance of himself at the party by shouting all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上整晚大喊大叫，很讨人嫌。
senses.why: Once annoyance has a name, that name easily shifts from the feeling to the person who reliably produces it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「烦扰」有了名字，这个名字很容易从那种感受转到总能制造出这种感受的人身上。

senses.title: A legal harm to the public
senses.definition: in law, an activity or condition that interferes with the public comfort or safety
senses.definitionCN: 法律上干扰公众安宁或安全的行为或状态
senses.example: The factory was sued for creating a public nuisance with its smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因排放烟雾构成妨害公众而被起诉。
senses.why: Because the earliest sense was plain harm, the law kept the word for conduct that harms a whole neighbourhood, not just one person.
senses.whyCN: 因为最早的意思就是「损害」，法律便保留这个词，用来指伤害整个街区而不只是某个人的行为。

intro.en: Nuisance came through French from a Latin verb for harming, and it still carries that original sting.
intro.cn: nuisance 经法语来自一个表示「伤害」的拉丁动词，至今还带着最初的那根刺。

items.en: Nocere meant to hurt or harm, and it is the root behind noxious and innocent as well.

items.en: Medieval Latin nocumentum named a harm or an injury done to someone.

items.en: Old French shortened the family to nuire, the verb for harming or annoying.
items.cn: 古法语把这族词简化为 nuire，即「伤害、烦扰」的动词。

items.en: The noun nuisance meant harm, annoyance and trouble in Old French.
items.cn: 名词 nuisance 在古法语中意为损害、烦扰与麻烦。

items.en: English borrowed it for annoyance of any kind and later gave it a precise legal sense.
items.cn: 英语借来泛指各种烦扰，后来又赋予它精确的法律含义。

normalIntro.en: The bone of the word is the Latin verb nocere, to harm, which is why nuisance grew from harm into annoyance and then into a legal wrong.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的骨头是拉丁语动词 nocere（伤害），所以 nuisance 从「损害」长成「烦扰」，再被法律固定成一种侵害。

normal.en: Nuisance and noxious share the Latin verb nocere, which means to harm.
normal.cn: nuisance 与 noxious 共用拉丁动词 nocere，意为伤害。

normal.en: The French noun moved from harm to mere annoyance, which is why the English word sounds milder than its root.
normal.cn: 法语名词从「损害」滑向「烦扰」，所以英语这个词听起来比它的词根温和。

normal.en: Innocent and innocuous add a negative prefix to the same root and turn harmful into harmless.
normal.cn: innocent 与 innocuous 在同一词根前加否定前缀，把「有害」变成「无害」。

normal.en: Public nuisance keeps the legal sense, naming conduct that harms a whole community.
normal.cn: public nuisance 保留法律义，指伤害整个社区的行为。

normal.en: Make a nuisance of oneself is the fixed phrase for a person who keeps bothering others.
normal.cn: make a nuisance of oneself 是固定说法，指不断给别人添烦的人。

abstract.en: A word for harm that softened into annoyance shows how often law and daily speech borrow from each other.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「伤害」的词软化成「烦扰」，正说明法律与日常语言常常互相借用。

abstract.en: Nuisance is small in scale but large in effect: one mosquito can cancel a whole night.
abstract.cn: nuisance 的规模很小，效果却很大：一只蚊子就能毁掉一整夜。

abstract.en: The same root that names poison also names harmlessness, depending on the prefix it wears.
abstract.cn: 给毒物命名的那个词根，也能给无害命名，全看它披着哪块前缀。

senses.title: Make someone accept a conclusion
senses.titleCN: 以论证使人接受某个结论
senses.definition: to cause a person to believe that something is true by presenting reasons
senses.definitionCN: 通过摆出理由，使某人相信某事为真
senses.example: The report persuaded the board that the old warehouse could be converted.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告使董事会相信，那座旧仓库可以改造。
senses.why: the oldest layer of the word is advice: per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'to advise' yields 'advise until the point is carried'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「进言」：per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」，合起来就是「劝到对方接受为止」。

senses.title: Urge someone to act
senses.definition: to talk someone into doing something they might not otherwise do
senses.definitionCN: 劝得某人去做他本不一定会做的事
senses.example: She persuaded her brother to take the later train.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服弟弟改乘晚一班火车。
senses.why: once the listener accepts the reasons, the next step is to move: advice about an act becomes advice to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 听者接受理由之后，下一步就是行动：关于「该怎么做」的进言，自然变成「去做」的劝使。

senses.title: Succeed where others failed
senses.titleCN: 把原本不肯的一方争取过来
senses.definition: to win over someone who has resisted argument, so that the attempt succeeds
senses.definitionCN: 把一直抗拒说理的一方争取过来，使劝说真正成功
senses.example: After two hours of argument he finally persuaded the holdouts.
senses.exampleCN: 争辩了两个小时，他终于说服了那几个坚持不让步的人。
senses.why: modern English treats persuade as a success verb: to say you persuaded someone is to say the person yielded.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把 persuade 当作「结果动词」：说「说服了某人」，就等于说对方已经让步。

senses.title: Win someone over by feeling
senses.titleCN: 靠情感打动而争取过来
senses.definition: to gain a person's agreement through warmth, charm or emotional appeal rather than proof
senses.definitionCN: 不靠证明，而以温情、魅力或情感打动来取得对方同意
senses.example: The singer's account persuaded even the reporters who had come to sneer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手的讲述甚至打动了本来打算嘲弄她的记者。
senses.why: suadere is generally thought to be tied to suavis 'sweet', so the word has always carried a hint of pleasantness as well as argument.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关，因此这个词除了论理，一直带着一点「可亲、顺耳」的意味。

senses.title: Come to believe after hearing
senses.titleCN: 被动义：听过之后转而相信
senses.definition: to become convinced of something oneself, especially in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 自己听过之后转为相信，多见于被动结构
senses.example: I was persuaded by the data, not by the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 让我信服的是数据，那番演讲并没有说服我。
senses.why: when the verb is passive, the listener moves to the side of the speaker, and the action is viewed from the receiving end.
senses.whyCN: 用于被动时，听者移到说话人这一边，动作便从「接受的一方」来看。

senses.title: Advise or urge strongly
senses.definition: to urge or advise a course of action forcefully, without implying that the advice was taken
senses.definitionCN: 强烈敦促或建议某种做法，不含「已被采纳」之意
senses.example: The old manuals persuade the reader to test each joint twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这些旧手册力劝读者把每个接缝都测两遍。
senses.why: seventeenth-century English used persuade where modern English would say urge; the success reading only became fixed later.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪的英语在今天的 urge 之处用 persuade；「成功」这层读法是后来才固定的。

senses.title: Talk oneself into believing
senses.definition: to bring oneself to accept something uncomfortable or doubtful
senses.definitionCN: 让自己接受某种令人不安或未必可靠的事
senses.example: He persuaded himself that the delay was harmless.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服自己相信这次延误并无妨碍。
senses.why: the mind can play both roles, speaker and listener, so the verb turns reflexive and describes inner bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 头脑可以同时扮演说话人与听者，于是这个动词转为自反，描述内心里的讨价还价。

senses.title: Swing a group as a whole
senses.definition: to change the decision of a body or assembly rather than a single person
senses.definitionCN: 使一个机构或集会整体改变决定，而非只改变一个人
senses.example: The petition persuaded the council to reopen the footpath.
senses.exampleCN: 请愿书使议会重新开放那条步道。
senses.why: a council votes as one voice, so persuading it means shifting the majority inside it.
senses.whyCN: 议会按一个声音投票，因此说服议会，实际上就是让其中的多数改向。

senses.title: Win people to a cause
senses.titleCN: 使人归附某种信念或事业
senses.definition: to convert people to a faith, party or cause one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个把人争取到某种信仰、党派或事业这一边
senses.example: Missionaries persuaded villagers one household at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 传教士一家一家地把村民争取过来。
senses.why: the same winning-over gesture, repeated person by person, becomes the language of conversion and recruitment.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「争取过来」的动作，一个人一个人地重复，就成了皈依与招纳的说法。

intro.en: Persuade entered English from Latin persuadere 'to urge thoroughly, prevail upon', built on per- 'thoroughly' and suadere 'to advise, urge'. Suadere is generally thought to be related to suavis 'sweet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: persuade 从拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」进入英语，由 per-「彻底」与 suadere「劝告、敦促」构成。一般认为 suadere 与 suavis「甜的」相关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Suadere meant 'to advise, recommend, urge'. The connection with suavis 'sweet, pleasant' is generally thought to be genuine, but the similarity alone does not prove it, and any deeper Indo-European shape for it exists only as a reconstructed form.
items.cn: suadere 意为「劝告、推荐、敦促」。它与 suavis「甜的、可亲的」的联系一般认为是真实的，但仅凭音形相近不足以证明；为它构拟的更早印欧形式只以重构形式存在。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere produced persuadere, 'to advise thoroughly, to prevail upon, to convince'. The prefix turns a piece of advice into an action carried through.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere 构成 persuadere，意为「劝到底、争取过来、使信服」。这个前缀把一句劝告变成一个做到底的动作。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the late fourteenth century, either taken straight from Latin or through Middle French persuader.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪晚期出现于英语，或直接取自拉丁语，或经中古法语 persuader 传入。

items.en: Early modern English still used the word for plain urging, where a modern writer would choose urge or advise; no success was implied.
items.cn: 早期现代英语仍用它表示单纯的「力劝」，今天的写作者会改用 urge 或 advise；当时并不含成功之意。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the success reading had settled in, and the passive 'be persuaded' became the ordinary way to report a change of mind.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「劝说成功」的读法已经固定，被动式「被说服」成为报告改变想法的常说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and deeper origin): the earliest dated example varies between dictionaries, and every pre-Latin form offered for suadere is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证与更深来源）：各家词典给出的最早年代并不一致；凡为 suadere 提出的拉丁语之前形式，都是重构形式，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look or sound close to persuade, one of which is not related at the root at all; group two gathers verbs that also move a listener but with a different lever.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，其中一个在词根上与本词毫无关系；第二组收同样能推动听者、但所用杠杆不同的动词。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus suadere, so it means to advise someone away from an action, the mirror image of persuade.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「离开」加 suadere，意为劝人不要做某事，正是 persuade 的镜像。

entries.definition: From Old French assouagier, from a Latin stem built on suavis 'sweet': to soften or soothe pain, sharing the sweet root but not the advising root.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语 assouagier，出自以 suavis「甜的」为基的拉丁词干：减轻、抚慰痛苦；与「甜」同根，却不走「劝告」这一支。

entries.tag: rare noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The formal noun from Latin suasio 'a advising', now mostly confined to the phrase moral suasion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 suasio「劝告」的正式名词，如今基本只用于「道义劝告」这一说法。

entries.definition: From Latin prosequi 'follow after', built on sequi 'to follow'; it looks close to persuade but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 prosequi「跟随」，由 sequi「跟随」构成；字形与 persuade 相近，词根却毫无关系。

entries.definition: To bring someone to accept a fact as true; the emphasis is on belief rather than on action.
entries.definitionCN: 使人接受某事实为真；侧重「相信」，而非「行动」。

entries.definition: To obtain something by gentle, patient urging; there is no argument, only smooth persistence.
entries.definitionCN: 靠温和耐心的劝哄取得某物；不讲道理，只靠柔和的坚持。

entries.definition: To influence a crowd or a decision, often through emotion; it is weaker on proof than persuade.
entries.definitionCN: 影响人群或决定，常借情感；在「论证」上比 persuade 弱。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for getting someone to agree by persistent asking, common in letters and speeches.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的「恳请」说法，靠一再请求使人同意，多见于书信与演说。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'advise': advice carried all the way through.
normal.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」：把劝告做到底。

normal.en: The family runs persuade, persuasion, persuasive, persuasively, persuasiveness, persuader.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persuade、persuasion、persuasive、persuasively、persuasiveness、persuader。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the two objects: persuade somebody to act, persuade somebody of a fact.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出两类宾语：劝人去做、使人相信某事实。

normal.en: The reverse verb is dissuade, built with the prefix that means apart.
normal.cn: 反向的动词是 dissuade，由表示「离开」的前缀构成。

normal.en: Passive reports are common: the committee was persuaded, the jury was persuaded.
normal.cn: 被动说法很常见：委员会被说服、陪审团被说服。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door that opens only after every key has been tried in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门，只有按顺序试过每一把钥匙才会开。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that tips only when a pebble is added to one side.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，只有在一侧再加一粒小石子时才倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a listener walking along a rope the speaker has laid out.
abstract.cn: 想象听者沿着说话人铺好的绳子往前走。

examples.en: Nothing could persuade the old farmer to sell the orchard.
examples.cn: 什么也无法说服那位老农卖掉果园。

examples.en: The teacher persuaded the class that the experiment was worth repeating.
examples.cn: 老师让全班相信这个实验值得重做一遍。

examples.en: He was persuaded only after he had read the original letters.
examples.cn: 他读过原始信件之后才被说服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（彻底）+ suade（劝）」——一直劝到对方彻底点头 → 说服

root: 拉丁 persuadere「劝到底、争取过来」= per-（彻底）+ suadere「劝告、敦促」；suadere 与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是同源，更深印欧形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: reasons are laid out, the listener is urged, belief settles, and belief turns into action or into a whole group changing course.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：先摆出理由，再向听者进言，信念落定，最后信念转为行动，或转为整群人改向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of reasons laid out on a table, along which a doubtful listener walks to the speaker's side.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上铺开一条理由的线，心存怀疑的听者沿着它走到说话人一边。

branches.en: ADVICE COMPLETED: the oldest layer is urging and advising, carried through to the end.
branches.cn: 把劝告做到底：最古老的一层是敦促与进言，一直做到终点。

branches.en: ACTION AND ASSEMBLY: a single listener is moved to act, then a whole council is moved to change course.
branches.cn: 行动与全体：先推动一个听者去做，再推动整个议会改向。

branches.en: BELIEF SURRENDERED: the resisting mind yields, and the passive form reports the change from the receiving side.
branches.cn: 信念让步：抗拒的一方松手，被动式则从接受方报告这一变化。

branches.en: SWEET PRESSURE: charm and warmth do the work that proof cannot do.
branches.cn: 甜的推力：证明做不到的事，由魅力与温情做到。

branches.en: INNER AND OUTER CONVERSION: the same voice persuades oneself, or persuades a household at a time.
branches.cn: 向内向外的皈依：同一个声音，可以劝服自己，也可以一家一家地劝服。

intro.en: Persuade is a Latin verb whose prefix and root still build English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: persuade 是一个拉丁动词，其前缀与词根至今仍在构成英语词，因此整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin suadere gives persuade, dissuade, suasion and assuage; the prefix per- adds the sense of doing something thoroughly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suadere 衍生 persuade、dissuade、suasion 与 assuage；前缀 per- 增添「彻底」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks the advice as carried through to success.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把关切标记为一直做到成功。

items.example: The root contributes the whole idea of advising.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贡献了「劝告」的全部意思。
那张图表说服了委员会。

items.example: A neighbour dissuaded him from signing.
items.exampleCN: 一位邻居劝他不要签字。

items.meaning: the act or result of persuading
items.example: The argument needed no further persuasion.
items.exampleCN: 这个论点无需再作说服。

items.example: She wrote a persuasive letter to the editor.
items.exampleCN: 她给编辑写了一封有说服力的信。

items.example: He argued persuasively for a second trial.
items.exampleCN: 他有力地为再次试验辩护。

items.example: The persuasiveness of the data surprised the panel.
items.exampleCN: 数据之有说服力让评审组意外。

items.example: The campaign relied on moral suasion.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动依靠道义劝告。

definition_zh: 申请；应用；使用；涂抹；敷用；适用；有效；努力；专心
definition_en: to make a formal request, to put something to use, to spread a substance, to be relevant, or to devote oneself to a task
core_image: 把一样东西贴到另一样东西上，让它起作用
scene: 面试房间外，年轻人把简历又理了一遍。 He decided to apply for the position as soon as it was advertised.
sceneCN: 这里 apply 是「申请」（第 1 个义项：向机构提出正式请求）；句意为「职位一公布，他就决定去申请」。画面里有面试房间外的走廊、年轻人与整理好的简历。

pos.zh: 动词：申请；应用；使用；涂抹；适用；努力；专心

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「申请；应用；应用程序」
由本词加 -ant 构成，义为「申请人」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「适用的；相关的」
由同一拉丁词根派生，义为「器具；家用电器」

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to make a formal request for a job, a place, a grant, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额、补助或许可提出正式请求
senses.example: She applied for a place in the design programme.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了设计专业的一个名额。
senses.why: Latin applicare first meant to attach oneself to something, and a request is the act of attaching yourself to a post.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 最初意为把自己贴附到某物上，而申请就是把自己附到一个职位上的动作。

senses.title: To put something to use
senses.definition: to use a rule, method, skill, or idea in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境中使用规则、方法、技能或想法
senses.example: Try to apply the same method to the next problem.
senses.exampleCN: 试着把同样的方法用到下一道题上。
senses.why: A method is folded onto a case, the way one layer is laid over another surface.
senses.whyCN: 方法被折叠到案例上，就像一层东西铺在另一层表面上。

senses.title: To spread on a surface
senses.definition: to spread or rub a substance such as cream, paint, or medicine onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把药膏、涂料或药物铺开、擦到某个表面上
senses.example: Apply the cream thinly twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 每天薄薄地涂两次药膏。
senses.why: This is applicare at its most physical: the substance is laid directly onto the skin.
senses.whyCN: 这是 applicare 最物理的用法：物质被直接铺到皮肤上。

senses.title: To be relevant
senses.definition: to be relevant to or valid for a person, case, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某案例或某情境相关并有效
senses.example: The rule applies to every member of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于队里的每一个人。
senses.why: Where a rule can be attached, it holds; being applicable is being able to be laid on the case.
senses.whyCN: 规则能被贴附到哪儿，就在哪儿生效；所谓适用，就是能被铺到那个案例上。

senses.title: To devote oneself
senses.definition: to work hard and give close attention to a task
senses.definitionCN: 努力工作并对一项任务保持专注
senses.example: If you apply yourself, the exam should go well.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你肯用功，这次考试应该会顺利。
senses.why: To apply oneself is to attach the whole mind to the task, leaving nothing loose.
senses.whyCN: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴到任务上，不留一点松散。

intro.en: Apply comes from the Latin verb of attaching, and every sense still carries that gesture.
intro.cn: apply 来自那个表示贴附的拉丁语动词，每个义项都还带着这个动作。

items.en: 「*plek-」 'to weave, fold' is the reconstructed root; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*plek-」意为「编织、折叠」，是重构的词根；更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold' supplies the physical image of one layer laid over another.
items.cn: plicare「折叠」提供了一层铺到另一层上的物理意象。

items.en: Ad- plus plicare formed applicare, 'to attach, put to, apply'.
items.cn: ad- 与 plicare 构成 applicare，意为「贴附、施加、应用」。

items.en: French aplier carries the verb into English, where it loses the final Latin ending.
items.cn: 法语 aplier 把这个动词带进英语，拉丁词尾在这里脱落。

items.en: The single verb spreads into requests, uses, coatings, relevance and hard study.
items.cn: 这一个动词铺开成申请、使用、涂抹、适用与用功。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun family built on apply; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of using, asking and spreading.
note.cn: 形近组收由 apply 构成的名词族；近义组收表示使用、请求与涂抹的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a request, a use, or a program.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词派生的名词，义为「申请、应用、程序」。

entries.definition: A person who makes a formal request.
entries.definitionCN: 提出正式申请的人，即「申请人」。

entries.definition: Relevant or able to be applied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适用的、相关的」。

entries.definition: A machine or device used for a household task.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「器具、家用电器」，与 apply 同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To employ something for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的而使用某物，对应 apply 的应用义。

entries.definition: To ask for something politely or formally.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌或正式地请求某物，对应 apply 的申请义。

entries.definition: To spread a substance messily over a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质抹到表面上，常带随意感，对应 apply 的涂抹义。

entries.definition: To give time and energy wholly to a task.
entries.definitionCN: 把时间与精力完全给出一项任务，对应 apply 的用功义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the single gesture of laying one thing onto another.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子始终围绕「把一物铺到另一物上」这一个动作。

normal.en: Apply is the verb; application is the noun made from it.
normal.cn: apply 是动词，application 是由它构成的名词。

normal.en: Apply for a job: attach yourself to a post.
normal.cn: apply for a job：把自己附到一个职位上。

normal.en: Apply a rule: lay it onto the case.
normal.cn: apply a rule：把规则铺到案例上。

normal.en: Apply cream: lay it onto the skin.
normal.cn: apply cream：把药膏敷到皮肤上。

normal.en: Apply yourself: lay your whole mind onto the work.
normal.cn: apply yourself：把整个心思铺到工作上。

abstract.en: One verb covers paper, method, medicine and effort.
abstract.cn: 一个动词覆盖纸张、方法、药物与努力。

abstract.en: Every sense answers the same question: what is being laid onto what.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在回答同一个问题：什么被铺到了什么上。

abstract.en: That is why the word feels both practical and moral.
abstract.cn: 所以这个词既实用，又带着一点品行意味。

examples.en: He decided to apply for the position as soon as it was advertised.
examples.cn: 职位一公布，他就决定去申请。

examples.en: Try to apply the same method to the next problem.
examples.cn: 试着把同样的方法用到下一道题上。

examples.en: Apply the cream thinly twice a day.
examples.cn: 每天薄薄地涂两次药膏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普莱」——把简历铺到桌上，贴向那个职位：申请；应用

root: apply 经古法语 aplier 来自拉丁语 applicare「贴附、施加」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 plicare「折叠」构成，更早的印欧词根形式存疑。这个词的核心动作始终是把一物铺到另一物上：把请求铺到职位上就是申请，把规则铺到案例上就是应用，把药膏铺到皮肤上就是涂抹，把心思铺到工作上就是用功。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses share one gesture: a request, a method, a cream, a rule and a mind are each laid onto something.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法共享一个动作：请求、方法、药膏、规则与心思，各自被铺到某个对象上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing one layer smoothly onto another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一层东西平整地按到另一层上。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: the self is attached to a position.
branches.cn: 职位线：自己被打附到一个职位上。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: a rule is laid onto a case.
branches.cn: 方法线：规则被铺到一个案例上。

branches.en: THE SKIN LINE: a substance is laid onto the body.
branches.cn: 皮肤线：物质被铺到身体上。

branches.en: THE VALIDITY LINE: what can be laid on a case holds there.
branches.cn: 有效线：能铺到某个案例上的规则，在那里就成立。

branches.en: THE EFFORT LINE: the mind itself is laid onto the task.
branches.cn: 努力线：心思本身被铺到任务上。

intro.en: Apply is a Latin verb stripped to an English shape, and its family is wide and transparent.
intro.cn: apply 是一个被削成英语外形的拉丁动词，它的词族宽而透明。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is genuine: applicare and plicare are the direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：applicare 与 plicare 是直接祖先。

items.meaning: to attach or put to use
items.example: They apply the paint with a small brush.
The applicant waited outside the office.
items.exampleCN: 申请人在办公室外等候。

items.example: This discount is applicable on weekdays.
items.exampleCN: 这个折扣在工作日可用。

items.meaning: a device put to household use
items.example: The kitchen appliance broke down again.
He will apply for a visa next month.

items.meaning: to concern or fit a case
items.example: The ban does not apply to visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这项禁令不适用于访客。

definition_zh: 确实；的确；实际上
definition_en: used to emphasize that something is true, or to add a stronger statement
core_image: 点了点头，又把手按在桌上补一句「真的」
scene: 别人怀疑你的说法时，你会加重语气再确认一次。 It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 indeed 是「确实」（第 1 个义项：强调所说的为真）；句意是那确实是全年最冷的一夜。

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「行为、事迹」，是本词的后半部分
义为「超过」，与 indeed 的 -ceed 部分形近，注意区分

senses.title: Emphasizing that something is true
senses.definition: used to make a statement stronger or to confirm it
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强或确认某个说法
senses.example: It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 那确实是全年最冷的一夜。
senses.why: The word is literally in deed, in the fact of the matter, so it points at reality itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在事实中」，所以它直接指向现实本身。

senses.title: Adding a stronger point
senses.titleCN: 而且：补上更进一步的说法
senses.definition: used to introduce a further and stronger piece of information
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步、更有力的信息
senses.example: He is a good teacher, indeed a great one.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位好老师，而且是一位了不起的老师。
senses.why: Confirming one fact opens the door to a bigger one, so the word also links escalations.
senses.whyCN: 确认一件事就打开了更大的门，因此这个词也用来连接递进。

senses.title: After very or an adjective, as intensifier
senses.titleCN: 非常：放在形容词后加强程度
senses.definition: placed after very and an adjective to strengthen the description
senses.definitionCN: 放在 very 加形容词之后，加强描述
senses.example: She was very tired indeed.
senses.exampleCN: 她确实非常累。
senses.why: At the end of a phrase the word becomes a stamp of emphasis, almost a nod.
senses.whyCN: 放在短语末尾时，它变成一枚强调的印章，几乎就是一个点头。

senses.title: Showing surprise or interest
senses.titleCN: 真的吗：表示惊讶或兴趣
senses.definition: used in speech to show mild surprise or to invite more talk
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示轻微的惊讶，或邀请对方继续讲
senses.example: Indeed? I had not heard about that.
senses.exampleCN: 真的吗？我还没听说过这事。
senses.why: The same confirmation becomes a question when the voice rises, a common speech habit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个确认词在语调上扬时就成了疑问，这是常见的口语习惯。

intro.en: Indeed is a Middle English compound of in and deed, meaning in fact or in reality.
intro.cn: indeed 是中古英语合成词，由 in 与 deed「行为、事实」构成，意为「在事实上」。

items.en: Dæd meant a deed or an act, the thing actually done.
items.cn: dæd 意为行为或事迹，即实际做出的事。

items.en: In dede was a phrase meaning in fact, written as one word later.
items.cn: in dede 是「事实上」的短语，后来写成一个词。

items.en: The word became a common way to confirm an assertion.
items.cn: 这个词成为确认论断的常用手段。

items.en: It also took the linking sense of a further, stronger point.
items.cn: 它也承担起引出更进一步说法的连接作用。

items.en: Spoken use added the surprised question, spoken with a rising tone.
items.cn: 口语用法又添上带上扬语调的惊讶疑问。

note.en: The look-alike group shares short in- words; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of emphasis and confirmation.
note.cn: 形近组收以 in- 开头的短词；近义组收表示强调与确认的副词。

entries.definition: An action that is done.
To start a line further from the margin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩进」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: An alphabetical list at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「索引」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: Without doubt.
In fact, used to correct a belief.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上」，常用于纠正看法。

entries.definition: In a genuine way.

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal in-deed reading, the sentence-final stamp and the rising question.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的 in-deed 结构、句末盖章与上扬疑问。

normal.en: In plus deed is in the deed, in what was actually done, so indeed means in fact.
normal.cn: in 加 deed 就是「在行为中」，即在真正做过的事里，所以意为「事实上」。

normal.en: A friend indeed is a friend in deeds, not merely in words, a proverb that explains the word.
normal.cn: a friend indeed 是「在行动上」的朋友而非只在嘴上，这句谚语正好解释这个词。

normal.en: Very tired indeed puts the nod at the end of the sentence.
normal.cn: very tired indeed 把那个点头放在句末。

normal.en: He is good, indeed great: the second statement is a step higher than the first.
normal.cn: He is good, indeed great：后一句比前一句又高了一级。

normal.en: Say it with a rising voice and the same word becomes really?
normal.cn: 把语调扬起来，同一个词就变成了「真的吗？」

abstract.en: Indeed is the shortest form of evidence: it points at the deed instead of describing it.
abstract.cn: indeed 是最短的证据形式：它指向行为，而不描述行为。

abstract.en: To confirm is a social act, so the word always assumes someone who doubted.
abstract.cn: 确认是一种社交行为，所以这个词总预设了一个曾怀疑的人。

abstract.en: A sentence ending in indeed leaves no room for the listener to disagree quietly.
abstract.cn: 以 indeed 收尾的句子，不留给听者悄悄反对的余地。

examples.en: Thank you very much indeed.
examples.cn: 真是非常感谢。

examples.en: The task was hard, indeed almost impossible.
examples.cn: 这项任务很难，几乎不可能完成。

examples.en: Indeed, the plan worked better than we hoped.
examples.cn: 的确，这计划比我们预想的更成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印底的」——印在纸底的那行字，的确是证据。

root: 中古英语 in（在）+ deed（行为、事实）→ in dede（事实上）→ indeed。

sensesIntro.en: Indeed starts as a pointer to a deed, becomes a stamp of truth, then a step up in argument, a sentence-final intensifier and finally a surprised question.
sensesIntro.cn: indeed 起初指向「行为」，后来成为真实的印章，再变成论述中的递进、句末的加强，最后成了惊讶的疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod of the head, then a hand pressed flat on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：先点头，再把手平按在桌上。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the word points at what really happened.
branches.cn: 真实线：这个词指向真正发生的事。

branches.en: ESCALATION LINE: the next claim goes one step further.
branches.cn: 递进线：下一个说法再进一层。

branches.en: STAMP LINE: placed after an adjective, it seals the description.
branches.cn: 盖章线：放在形容词后，为描述封口。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: a rising tone turns it into a question.
branches.cn: 口语线：上扬的语调把它变成疑问。

branches.en: RHETORIC LINE: confirming first makes a bigger claim easier to accept.
branches.cn: 修辞线：先确认小事，大话更容易被接受。

intro.en: A preposition fused with an Old English noun of action, plus a short family of -deed words.
intro.cn: 一个介词与一个古英语行为名词熔成一词，外加一族简短的 -deed 词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalent structure is in facto, in the fact, which also gives English fact and feat.
latinIntro.cn: 对应的拉丁结构是 in facto「在事实中」，英语由此得到 fact 与 feat。

items.example: He said so, and indeed so it was.
items.exampleCN: 他这么说，事实也确是如此。

items.meaning: in action, not only in words
items.meaningCN: 在行动上，而不只在口头上
items.example: help in deed as well as in word

items.meaning: a document that transfers a gift
